﻿M3-T11-180 — Unit-median fresh-Sigma divisor compression and symmetric conductor amplification


CARD_ID: M3-T11-180
CANONICAL_CARD_KEY: M3-T11-180
STATUS: PROVED_K1_FIXED_FRESH_SIGMA_FIBER / PROVED_K1_SUMMED_SMALL_FRESH_SIGMA_SECTOR / QUANTIFIED_SYMMETRIC_CONDUCTOR_ROUTER / GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT=0
PRIMARY_GATE: M3-T11-GATE-001, OPEN
GLOBAL_OPERATION: ACTIVE_T11_RESEARCH_WITH_SCOPED_DECOMPOSITION
GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT: 0
AUDIT_MODE: WITHIN_SESSION_DEDUCTIVE_FROM_RETAINED_015_016_036_039_040_042A_171_176_177_179


1. Current authority and decision


Fresh MAIN, CARD-INDEX, current short RESULT-LEDGER, active ROUTE and M3-T11-179 were read first. Retained M3-T11-015/016/019/023/024/029/030/035/036/039/040/041/042-A/042-B/043/171/176/177 were checked only where needed.


Direct multiplication of the two large one-core M3-T11-026 root-line densities is not allowed. M3-T11-019/023/024 and M3-T11-040/041 already impose no-double-charge constraints on precisely these shared endpoint selectors.


Instead, the K=1 structure gives a canonical physical divisor coordinate that absorbs the moving content and the two-smallest fresh relative cores at once.


For every K=1 endpoint, after deterministic relabeling,
(h_1,h_2,h_3)=(1,1,h),
R=h*tau,
1<=h<=R<=B.


Write the relative norms
tau_i=m_i*n_i, i=1,2,3,
where m_i=tau_i^sharp is the relative fresh part supported outside the rational prime support of h, and n_i is h-supported. Sort
m_(1)<=m_(2)<=m_(3)
with deterministic tie breaking by original relative-core label.


Define the fresh content-weighted two-core divisor
Sigma_sharp := h*m_(1)*m_(2).                       (180.1)


The main result is:
- Sigma_sharp is an actual divisor of the physical R;
- every fixed Sigma_sharp fiber has B^o(1) exact physical endpoints;
- therefore the whole sector Sigma_sharp<=B^(1/3-delta) is negligible for every fixed delta>0.


On the remaining small-c K=1 branch this forces a stronger full fresh conductor and quantitatively activates the retained symmetric S/u conductor router.


No global endpoint upper bound or closure of M3-T11-GATE-001 is claimed.


2. Sigma_sharp is a physical divisor


Since m_(1) and m_(2) divide two of the pairwise-coprime relative norms tau_1,tau_2,tau_3, their product divides
tau_1*tau_2*tau_3 | tau.


Therefore
Sigma_sharp=h*m_(1)*m_(2) | h*tau=R.                (180.2)


In particular
1<=Sigma_sharp<=R<=B.                                (180.3)


This is not an auxiliary root-line modulus. It is a canonical same-endpoint integer divisor of the terminal diagonal.


3. Uniform fixed-Sigma_sharp endpoint fiber


Fix
Sigma_sharp=N<=B.


Choose the two original relative-core labels a,b that realize the deterministic two-smallest fresh norms. There are at most three label-pair choices.


The positive integers
(h,m_a,m_b)
satisfy
h*m_a*m_b=N.                                         (180.4)


Hence the number of ordered triples is at most d_3(N)=N^o(1).


For each such h,m_a,m_b, write
tau_a=m_a*n_a,
tau_b=m_b*n_b,
with rad(n_a*n_b)|h and physical polynomial height.


The support-restricted integer lemma proved in M3-T11-177 gives uniformly
#{n<=B^A:rad(n)|h}=B^o(1)                            (180.5)
for every fixed A and all h<=B. Thus the pair (n_a,n_b), hence the full norm pair (tau_a,tau_b), has only B^o(1) possibilities.


For K=1 the coefficient norms are (h,h,1). Their primitive Gaussian representations, unit choices and parity/orientation choices cost B^o(1).


After the coefficient packet and the two full relative cores G_a,G_b are fixed, retained M3-T11-016 gives only B^o(1) endpoint-compatible possibilities for the third relative core G_j. Retained M3-T11-015 then gives only O(1) compatible all-same core G_0. The degenerate phase pairs excluded in M3-T11-016 remain physically empty.


All sphere, triple-spin, torus double-lift, face-integrality, M3-T11-176 denominator, primitivity and canonical-order conditions remain exact post-filters.


Consequently, uniformly for N<=B,
m_SigmaSharp(N;B)
:=#{exact primitive canonical K=1 endpoints R<=B with Sigma_sharp=N}
<=B^o(1).                                            (180.6)


No outer content factor remains. The content h has been absorbed into the divisor label N.


4. Summed small-Sigma_sharp sector


For every 1<=Z<=B,
P_K1,SigmaSharp<=Z(B)
<=Z*B^o(1).                                          (180.7)


Choose any fixed delta_sharp>0 and set
Z=B^(1/3-delta_sharp).                               (180.8)


Using the retained lower benchmark M3(B)>>B^(1/3),
P_K1,SigmaSharp<=Z(B)
<=B^(1/3-delta_sharp+o(1))
=o(M3(B)).                                           (180.9)


This disposal is valid on the entire K=1 population, before imposing c_max<=C.


It strictly strengthens the M3-T11-179 summation receiver. M3-T11-179 paid the outer h<=C factor and removed
m_(1)m_(2)<=B^(1/6-xi-epsilon_2).
Here the condition is
h*m_(1)m_(2)<=B^(1/3-delta_sharp),                   (180.10)
which can allow much larger m_(1)m_(2) when h is small. M3-T11-179 remains correct but its small-two-fresh-product sector is subsumed by the fresh-Sigma receiver after compatible parameter choices.


5. Residual fresh-core balance on the live small-c K=1 branch


Now impose the live small-c bound
h<=C=B^(1/6+xi).


After removing (180.9), every remaining K=1 endpoint satisfies
h*m_(1)m_(2)>B^(1/3-delta_sharp).                    (180.11)


Hence exactly
m_(1)m_(2)
>B^(1/3-delta_sharp)/h.                              (180.12)


Uniformly using h<=C,
m_(1)m_(2)
>B^(1/6-delta_sharp-xi).                             (180.13)


Therefore
m_(2),m_(3)
>B^(1/12-delta_sharp/2-xi/2).                        (180.14)


More importantly, because m_(3)>=m_(2)>=sqrt(m_(1)m_(2)),
M_rel=m_1*m_2*m_3
> (B^(1/3-delta_sharp)/h)^(3/2).                    (180.15)


Thus the exact h-sensitive full-fresh lower bound is
M_rel
>B^(1/2-(3/2)delta_sharp)/h^(3/2),                  (180.16)
and uniformly on h<=C,
M_rel
>B^(1/4-(3/2)delta_sharp-(3/2)xi).                  (180.17)


This explicit full-M_rel amplification was not recorded in M3-T11-179.


6. Quantified symmetric S/u conductor router


Retained M3-T11-036 is hostile-audit-passed and gives B^o(1) physical multiplicity on fixed realized S and fixed realized u inside one content/coefficient packet.


Retained M3-T11-039/040 define
Q_S=gcd(Den(S),M_rel^2),
C_u=gcd(A_u^2+B_u^2,M_rel^4)/M_rel^2
for reduced u=A_u/B_u, and prove exactly
Q_S*C_u=M_rel^2.                                     (180.18)


Therefore every endpoint on the residual satisfies the deterministic dichotomy
max(Q_S,C_u)>=M_rel.                                 (180.19)


By (180.16), at the exact h-sensitive level,
max(Q_S,C_u)
>B^(1/2-(3/2)delta_sharp)/h^(3/2).                  (180.20)


Uniformly on h<=C,
max(Q_S,C_u)
>B^(1/4-(3/2)delta_sharp-(3/2)xi).                  (180.21)


Thus the K=1 residual routes to one of two canonical same-measure extreme branches:


S-branch:
Q_S>=M_rel, so the reduced denominator of S contains a fresh divisor exceeding the bound in (180.20)/(180.21).


u-branch:
C_u>=M_rel. Retained M3-T11-039 gives
gcd(A_u^2+B_u^2,M_rel^4)
=M_rel^2*C_u
>=M_rel^3.                                           (180.22)


Hence on the u-branch the common-u Gaussian norm carries fresh content
>B^(3/2-(9/2)delta_sharp)/h^(9/2)                   (180.23)
in the exact h-sensitive form, and uniformly
>B^(3/4-(9/2)delta_sharp-(9/2)xi).                  (180.24)


These are conductor statements, not support-counting savings.


7. Fourth-power middle-denominator marker


Retained M3-T11-042-A proves exactly
M_rel^4 | Den(E)                                    (180.25)
for the symmetric middle coefficient E.


Combining with (180.16),
Den(E)
>B^(2-6delta_sharp)/h^6.                             (180.26)


Uniformly on h<=C,
Den(E)
>B^(1-6delta_sharp-6xi).                             (180.27)


This near-B-scale denominator is a useful quantitative marker of the residual when delta_sharp+xi is small.


However M3-T11-042-A explicitly states that M_rel^4|Den(E) is a recombination of the same S/u conductor allocation, not an independent saving. Equation (180.27) receives zero extra counting credit.


8. Why the direct dual-root-line density route is not credited


M3-T11-179 guarantees two large distinct one-core squared moduli. That remains true.


But:
- M3-T11-019 gives charged-once Plucker eliminants and explicitly forbids multiplying its determinant by already-paid core spacing;
- M3-T11-023 uses one shared auxiliary modulus and forbids tensorizing it into independent core moduli;
- M3-T11-024 reduces the selector to one paired-Gaussian common-core principal-squareclass problem, not two independent detectors;
- M3-T11-040/041 prove that the symmetric S/u allocations are complementary pieces of one M_rel^2 conductor.


Therefore no valid fixed-power gain follows merely by multiplying the two large M3-T11-026 root-line densities. The new progress in this card is instead the exact fresh-Sigma divisor fiber and the resulting quantitative conductor amplification.


The two large relative moduli remain available as structural selectors for any future genuinely same-endpoint correlation theorem.


9. Occupied-support formulation


Let S_SigmaSharp(B) be the actually occupied values of Sigma_sharp on the K=1 endpoint population.


Because every occupied value has at least one endpoint and (180.6) gives B^o(1) multiplicity,
|S_SigmaSharp(B)|
<= #E_K1(B)
<= B^o(1)|S_SigmaSharp(B)|.                          (180.28)


Thus K=1 endpoint counting and occupied fresh-Sigma support have the same power exponent.


A rigorously sufficient support target is
|S_SigmaSharp(B)| << B^(1/3-epsilon)                 (180.29)
for some fixed epsilon>0.


No such large-Sigma_sharp support deficit is proved here.


10. Novelty and limits


CARD-INDEX searches for fresh Sigma, Sigma sharp, content-weighted fresh, fresh divisor coordinate, two-smallest fresh divisor, fixed fresh Sigma, Q_S C_u K=1 and large symmetric conductor K=1 found no prior card stating (180.1)-(180.9) or the quantified K=1 specialization (180.20)-(180.27).


M3-T11-171 is the closest retained theorem, but it uses the two smallest FULL relative norms and Sigma=H*tau_(1)*tau_(2). The present coordinate uses FRESH relative parts and exploits the K=1 content-supported nonfresh compression from M3-T11-177.


No large-Sigma_sharp support deficit, no S-denominator tail, no amplified-u norm tail and no global endpoint bound are proved. No independent hostile audit and no physical endpoint enumeration are claimed.

11. Drive-only handoff


LATEST_RESEARCH_CARD=M3-T11-180
NEXT_CANDIDATE=M3-T11-181
CURRENT_ATTACK=LargeFreshSigmaSupportOrSymmetricExtremeTail


181 should work on the residual
Sigma_sharp=h*m_(1)m_(2)>B^(1/3-delta_sharp)
with exact Sigma_sharp|R.


Two legitimate next routes are:
(A) a same-measure occupied-support deficit for the canonical divisor Sigma_sharp;
(B) the symmetric extreme router from (180.18)-(180.24): large Q_S denominator support versus large C_u amplified common-u Gaussian norm.


For route (B), fixed-S and fixed-u fibers are already B^o(1) by audited M3-T11-036, but a moving-support/tail theorem is still required. The M3-T11-042-A fourth-power E denominator is only a marker and cannot be charged independently.


Retain M3-T11-176 exact two-unit denominator filters, large Sigma/large D_min, full triple-spin and torus double-lift selectors, and the two large relative M3-T11-026 moduli from179.

﻿M3-T11-179 — Unit-median two-smallest fresh-relative product disposal and dual large-modulus residual


CARD_ID: M3-T11-179
CANONICAL_CARD_KEY: M3-T11-179
STATUS: PROVED_K1_SMALL_TWO_FRESH_PRODUCT_ENDPOINT_SECTOR / PROVED_K1_TWO_LARGE_RELATIVE_FRESH_CORES / GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT=0
PRIMARY_GATE: M3-T11-GATE-001, OPEN
GLOBAL_OPERATION: ACTIVE_T11_RESEARCH_WITH_SCOPED_DECOMPOSITION
GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT: 0
AUDIT_MODE: WITHIN_SESSION_DEDUCTIVE_FROM_RETAINED_015_016_030_171_176_177_178


1. Current authority and decision


Fresh MAIN, CARD-INDEX, current short RESULT-LEDGER, active ROUTE and M3-T11-178 were read first. Retained M3-T11-015/016/017/026/029/030/032/033/171/176/177 were checked only where needed.


Work on the exact K=1 subpopulation of the live small-c branch:
c_max<=C=B^(1/6+xi),
h_middle=1,
R<=B,
with large Sigma, large D_min, full Gaussian orientation, triple-spin, torus double-lift, M3-T11-176 denominator filters and all physical endpoint masks retained.


After deterministic relabeling,
(h_1,h_2,h_3)=(1,1,h), 1<=h<=C,
and the content-prime support is
S_h={p:p|h}.


Write the three relative core norms as
tau_i=m_i*n_i, i=1,2,3,                         (179.1)
where m_i=tau_i^sharp is the fresh part supported outside S_h and n_i is S_h-supported. The m_i are pairwise coprime because the full relative norms tau_i are pairwise coprime.


Sort the fresh relative norms
m_(1)<=m_(2)<=m_(3),                              (179.2)
breaking ties by the smallest original relative-core label.


The new result is that the entire endpoint sector with small product of the two smallest fresh relative norms is negligible after paying the full K=1 content family. Therefore every surviving K=1 endpoint has TWO polynomially large relative fresh cores, not merely one.


No global endpoint upper bound or closure of the primary gate is claimed.


2. Fixed fresh-pair endpoint fiber


Fix:
- the K=1 content h;
- two distinct relative-core labels a,b;
- two positive fresh norms m_a,m_b.


For each selected label k in {a,b}, the nonfresh factor n_k in (179.1) is supported on primes dividing h and is bounded by the physical polynomial height.


The support-restricted integer lemma proved in M3-T11-177 gives uniformly for fixed h<=C:
#{n<=B^A : rad(n)|h}=B^o(1)                    (179.3)
for every fixed A.


Hence the number of possible pairs (n_a,n_b), and therefore full norm pairs
(tau_a,tau_b)=(m_a n_a,m_b n_b),                (179.4)
is B^o(1).


For every such full pair:
- the coefficient norms are (h,h,1), so the Gaussian coefficient packet has B^o(1) choices;
- primitive Gaussian cores G_a,G_b of norms tau_a,tau_b have B^o(1) choices by the sum-of-two-squares divisor bound;
- retained M3-T11-016 gives B^o(1) endpoint-compatible choices for the third relative core G_j after the packet,G_a,G_b are fixed;
- retained M3-T11-015 then gives only O(1) compatible all-same core G_0 after the three relative cores and packet are fixed.


The M3-T11-016 degenerate phase pairs are physically empty exactly as in that retained theorem, so there is no exceptional polynomial family.


Therefore, uniformly for fixed (h,a,b,m_a,m_b),
#{exact primitive canonical K=1 endpoints with these data}
<=B^o(1).                                           (179.5)


All triple-spin, double-lift, face-integrality, exact M3-T11-176 denominator, primitivity and canonical-order conditions are retained or applied as post-filters. Equation (179.5) is a same-physical-measure fiber theorem.


3. Summed small two-fresh-product sector


Let
M_2^fresh := m_(1)m_(2).                            (179.6)


For a fixed h, the number of ordered positive integer pairs (u,v) with uv<=Y is
sum_{u<=Y} floor(Y/u)
<=Y(1+log Y)
=Y B^o(1).                                          (179.7)


The deterministic labels of the two smallest fresh cores cost at most three choices. Combining (179.5)-(179.7) and summing h<=C gives, uniformly for 1<=Y<=B^2,
#E_K1,M2fresh<=Y(B;C)
<=C*Y*B^o(1).                                       (179.8)


No ambient root-line density is used. The third relative core is summed through the retained fixed-two-core elliptic fiber theorem, not through an unrestricted integer range.


Choose a fixed epsilon_2>0 with xi+epsilon_2<1/6 and set
Y=B^(1/6-xi-epsilon_2).                             (179.9)


Then, since C=B^(1/6+xi),
#E_K1,M2fresh<=Y
<=B^(1/3-epsilon_2+o(1))
=o(M3(B)).                                          (179.10)


Thus the entire exact K=1 endpoint sector
m_(1)m_(2)<=B^(1/6-xi-epsilon_2)                   (179.11)
is negligible.


4. Relation to M3-T11-178 and M3-T11-171


Because
M_rel=m_1m_2m_3
and m_(3)>=1,
M_rel<=Y implies m_(1)m_(2)<=Y.                     (179.12)


Therefore for the same numerical cutoff, the small-M_rel sector disposed in M3-T11-178 is contained in the new sector (179.11). M3-T11-178 remains correct, but its small-M_rel disposal is superseded for the K=1 continuation by (179.10).


M3-T11-171 is different. It controls
Sigma=H*tau_(1)tau_(2)
using the two smallest FULL relative norms. The present theorem controls the two smallest FRESH relative parts after all S_h-supported prime powers are summed at B^o(1) cost. It is therefore a fresh-conductor refinement, not a restatement of the small-Sigma sector.


5. Two large relative fresh cores on the residual


After removing (179.10), every remaining K=1 endpoint satisfies
m_(1)m_(2)>Y.                                       (179.13)


Since m_(1)<=m_(2)<=m_(3),
m_(2)^2 >= m_(1)m_(2)>Y.                            (179.14)


Hence
m_(2),m_(3)
>B^(1/12-xi/2-epsilon_2/2).                         (179.15)


In particular, at least two distinct relative fresh cores carry polynomial size at this stronger scale.


For each k in the two largest fresh-core labels, retained M3-T11-026 supplies the actual squared Gaussian ideal modulus
mathfrak_M_k=(G_k^sharp)^2
with
N(mathfrak_M_k)=m_k^2.


Therefore every surviving endpoint carries TWO distinct relative squared-modulus selectors satisfying
N(mathfrak_M_k)
>B^(1/6-xi-epsilon_2),                              (179.16)
for k corresponding to m_(2) and m_(3).


The two moduli are coprime because the fresh relative cores are pairwise coprime.


This is a structural dual-large-conductor statement only. The two modulus conditions are correlated through the same endpoint and must not be multiplied as independent probabilities.


6. Same-measure dual root-line formulation


For each of the two large relative fresh cores, retained corrected M3-T11-029 gives its own distinct rational anti-root
v_k=A_k/B_k
and primitive oriented root line
A_k == rho_k B_k mod m_k^2,
rho_k^2 == -1 mod m_k^2,
gcd(B_k,m_k)=1.                                     (179.17)


The two anti-roots are distinct coordinates; the withdrawn common-v CRT claim from the old M3-T11-030 is not used.


The M3-T11-032/033 product-cubic coefficient pair may package all three root lines algebraically, but its exact product-factorization addendum shows that this carries no independent density credit. Accordingly the live K=1 residual should be viewed as a TWO-coordinate correlated root-line/principal-incidence problem, with each of two moduli already at norm scale (179.16).


Retain simultaneously:
- exact M3-T11-176 two-unit denominator filters;
- large Sigma and large D_min;
- full triple-spin principal-square relation;
- torus double-lift selector;
- exact physical R<=B, positivity, primitivity and canonical ordering.


7. What this changes in the live K=1 problem


M3-T11-178 reduced the residual to one guaranteed large relative fresh core.


M3-T11-179 strengthens this to two guaranteed large relative fresh cores. The current K=1 residual is therefore:


UnitMedianDualLargeRelativeFreshPhysicalSupport.


Quantitatively:
m_(1)m_(2)>B^(1/6-xi-epsilon_2),                    (179.18)
m_(2),m_(3)>B^(1/12-xi/2-epsilon_2/2),              (179.19)
N(mathfrak_M_(2)),N(mathfrak_M_(3))
>B^(1/6-xi-epsilon_2).                               (179.20)


The useful next theorem must exploit a SAME-ENDPOINT correlation between these two large relative selectors and the principal/double-lift physical conditions. A product of two separate one-core density estimates is prohibited.


8. Novelty and limits


CARD-INDEX searches for two-smallest fresh, fresh pair product, fixed two fresh cores, small fresh pair and relative fresh pair found no prior card stating (179.5)-(179.10).


M3-T11-016 supplied the fixed-two FULL core elliptic fiber, but did not sum moving fresh pairs or moving content. M3-T11-030 compressed S_content-supported factors for fixed packets, but did not omit the third relative core through M3-T11-016. M3-T11-171 summed two smallest FULL core norms with the physical content product, not fresh relative parts.


No count is proved for the dual-large residual. No independence of the two squared moduli is asserted. The result is deductive from retained exact structure and retained uniform fixed-two-core counting; no physical endpoint enumeration and no independent hostile audit are claimed.

NEXT_CANDIDATE=M3-T11-180
CURRENT_ATTACK=UnitMedianDualLargeRelativeFreshPhysicalCorrelation

Use the two deterministic large relative fresh-core labels simultaneously, but preserve their distinct anti-root coordinates. Combine:
- the two M3-T11-026 squared Gaussian ideal incidences;
- the two corrected M3-T11-029 primitive root lines;
- M3-T11-019 Plucker eliminants or M3-T11-023/024 principal-incidence structure only if the same physical weights and quantifier order are preserved;

Do not multiply two one-core local densities, do not resurrect the common-v CRT, do not charge the M3-T11-032/033 product coefficient pair independently, and do not replace the endpoint measure by an ambient pair of residue boxes.

No global endpoint upper bound or closure of M3-T11-GATE-001 is claimed.


2. Relative fresh conductor on K=1


For one exact Step-A content/coefficient packet use the retained four-core notation
tau=tau_0*tau_1*tau_2*tau_3,

This is a new scoped endpoint disposal. It includes all possible tau_0, including a very large all-same fresh core, and includes all S_content-supported prime powers in the three relative cores through N_rel.


4. Relation to M3-T11-177

Thus with the same numerical cutoff, the 177 small-tau^sharp sector is contained in the new small-M_rel sector. M3-T11-177 remains correct, but its small-fresh disposal is strictly superseded for the K=1 continuation by (178.8).

with

>B^(1/9-(2/3)xi-(2/3)epsilon_M).                    (178.13)


This relative squared-modulus carrier exists regardless of whether tau_0^sharp is smaller or larger than m_i. Thus the M3-T11-027 maximal-core dichotomy is no longer needed as the PRIMARY K=1 router after (178.8).


The all-same square-divisor theorem remains valid as an additional exact endpoint selector whenever G_0^sharp is large. It is not retracted and receives no independent counting credit here.

Accordingly (178.15) may be used as a structural conductor/range marker, but no saving may be multiplied on top of the individual relative root-line conditions merely because the product modulus is large.


The withdrawn common-v CRT statement of the old M3-T11-030 is also not used.

(B) maximal all-same fresh core -> Gaussian numerator square divisor.


After (178.8), every residual endpoint already has polynomially large M_rel. Therefore one can ALWAYS select a polynomially large relative fresh core and invoke M3-T11-026.

UnitMedianLargeRelativeFreshPhysicalSupport.

﻿M3-T11-177 — Unit-median occupied-tau collapse and small-fresh sector disposal


CARD_ID: M3-T11-177
CANONICAL_CARD_KEY: M3-T11-177
STATUS: PROVED_K1_OCCUPIED_TAU_RECEIVER_COLLAPSE / PROVED_K1_SMALL_FRESH_ENDPOINT_SECTOR / LARGE_FRESH_CONDUCTOR_REDUCTION / GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT=0
PRIMARY_GATE: M3-T11-GATE-001, OPEN
GLOBAL_OPERATION: ACTIVE_T11_RESEARCH_WITH_SCOPED_DECOMPOSITION
GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT: 0
AUDIT_MODE: WITHIN_SESSION_DEDUCTIVE_FROM_RETAINED_014_017_027_169_171_174_176


1. Current authority and decision


Fresh MAIN, CARD-INDEX, current short RESULT-LEDGER, active ROUTE and M3-T11-176 were read first. Retained M3-T11-014/017/027/169/171/174 were checked only where needed.


Work on the exact K=1 subpopulation of the live small-c branch:
c_max<=C=B^(1/6+xi),
h_middle=1,
R>B^(2/3-eta),
Sigma>B^(1/3-delta_Sigma),
D_min>B^(1/3-delta_D),
with all full Gaussian orientations, triple-spin, torus double lift, M3-T11-176 denominator filters and physical endpoint masks retained.


Since contents are positive and h_middle=1, after deterministic relabeling the sorted content triple is
(h_a,h_b,h_c)=(1,1,h), 1<=h<=C.
Thus H=h, c_max=h, and M3-T11-174 gives
q_min=tau,
D_min=tau,
R=h*tau.                                             (177.1)


The first new point is that the K=1 receiver can be indexed by tau alone: the outer h<=C factor in the M3-T11-176 content-packet receiver is not intrinsic once M3-T11-174 is used.


The second new point is a genuine endpoint-sector disposal. In the K=1 packet, the old/nonfresh part of tau has prime support inside 2h. Such integers have only B^o(1) possibilities for fixed h. Therefore a small fresh part can be summed with its full content cost, producing a power-saving endpoint sector.


No global endpoint upper bound follows. The large-fresh K=1 residual remains open.


2. Fixed-tau receiver collapse at K=1


M3-T11-174 proves uniformly for every integer d<=B
#{primitive positive canonical endpoints R<=B with D_min=d} <= B^o(1).       (174.1)


By (177.1), every K=1 endpoint with common residual tau=n lies in the fixed-D_min fiber d=n. Hence uniformly
m_tau^(K=1)(n;B)
:=#{K=1 endpoints with tau=n}
<=B^o(1).                                             (177.2)


Let S_tau^(1)(B;C) be the actually occupied tau values in the exact K=1 small-c branch, with all retained large-Sigma, large-D_min and physical masks. Then
|S_tau^(1)| <= #E_K1(B;C) <= B^o(1)|S_tau^(1)|.       (177.3)


Thus K=1 endpoint counting and occupied-tau support have the same power exponent. A rigorously sufficient support target is
|S_tau^(1)(B;C)| << B^(1/3-epsilon)
for some fixed epsilon>0.                              (177.4)


This supersedes only the choice of receiver in M3-T11-176 Section 5 for K=1. Its per-content target B^(1/6-xi-epsilon) remains sufficient, but it is not minimal after (177.2). No analogous collapse is claimed for K>1, where D_min=q_min*h_middle retains the median-content coordinate.


3. Two strengthened lower bounds on the K=1 residual


First, retained large R and R=h*tau with h<=C give
tau=R/h > B^(2/3-eta)/C
           = B^(1/2-eta-xi).                          (177.5)


This is stronger than the general small-c tau lower bound on the current fixed-small-parameter branch.


Second, M3-T11-171 gives on the residual
Sigma=H*tau_(1)*tau_(2)>B^(1/3-delta_Sigma),
where tau_(1)<=tau_(2)<=tau_(3) are the three relative-core norms. Since H=h<=C,
tau_(1)*tau_(2)
> B^(1/3-delta_Sigma)/C
= B^(1/6-delta_Sigma-xi).                              (177.6)


Therefore
tau_(2), tau_(3)
> B^(1/12-delta_Sigma/2-xi/2).                        (177.7)


This is the unit-median specialization of the full-relative-core balance, improving the general small-c exponent from M3-T11-171. It is a necessary condition only; no independent savings are multiplied.


4. Fresh/nonfresh factorization at unit median


For contents (1,1,h), the three coefficient norms in M3-T11-176 are
(c_1,c_2,c_3)=(h,h,1)
up to relabeling, so
c_1*c_2*c_3=h^2.                                      (177.8)


Use the exact M3-T11-027 definition: tau^sharp is the part of tau supported on odd split rational primes not dividing the fixed content product. Retained M3-T11-014 says every odd prime dividing tau (indeed every odd prime dividing R) is 1 mod 4. Therefore if
tau=tau^sharp*tau_old,                                 (177.9)
then
rad(tau_old) | 2h.                                     (177.10)


The factors in (177.9) are the canonical support split; tau^sharp is odd and coprime to h.


5. Uniform support-restricted integer lemma


Lemma. Fix any constant A>0. Uniformly for integers 1<=m<=B^A,
#{n<=B : rad(n)|m}=B^o(1).                            (177.11)


Proof. Put k=omega(m). Since the product of the first k primes is at least k!, m<=B^A implies
k=O_A(log B/log log B).


Take sigma=(log log B)^(-1/2). Rankin's trick gives
#{n<=B:rad(n)|m}
<= B^sigma * sum_{rad(n)|m} n^(-sigma)
= B^sigma * product_{p|m}(1-p^(-sigma))^(-1).


Uniformly for p>=2 and small positive sigma,
(1-p^(-sigma))^(-1) <= C0/sigma
with an absolute C0. Hence the logarithm of the Euler product is
O(k log(1/sigma))=o(log B),
while sigma log B=o(log B). This proves (177.11).


Only this elementary support count is used. No distribution of primes or independent local density is asserted.


6. Small-fresh K=1 endpoint sector


Fix h<=C and s=tau^sharp. By (177.10)-(177.11), the number of possible tau_old<=B, hence the number of possible tau=s*tau_old<=B, is B^o(1), uniformly in h and s.


For each fixed labeled content triple (1,1,h) and fixed tau, retained M3-T11-017 gives B^o(1) exact endpoint candidates. Equivalently, after tau is fixed one may also use the stronger K=1 fixed-D_min fiber (177.2).


Therefore for every 1<=F<=B,
#E_K1,tau^sharp<=F(B;C)
<= C * F * B^o(1).                                    (177.12)


At C=B^(1/6+xi), choose a fixed epsilon_f>0 and
F=B^(1/6-xi-epsilon_f).                               (177.13)


Then
#E_K1,tau^sharp<=F
<=B^(1/3-epsilon_f+o(1))
=o(M3(B)),                                             (177.14)
using the retained benchmark M3(B)>>B^(1/3).


This is a genuine scoped endpoint disposal on the exact physical measure. It includes the entire moving nonfresh prime-power part of tau, the content sum h<=C, all coefficient orientations and every retained endpoint mask. It does not use the R502 raw carrier.


7. Large-fresh residual and M3-T11-027 reactivation


After removing (177.14), every remaining K=1 endpoint satisfies
tau^sharp > B^(1/6-xi-epsilon_f).                     (177.15)


Retained M3-T11-027 decomposes
tau^sharp=tau_0^sharp*tau_1^sharp*tau_2^sharp*tau_3^sharp
into pairwise coprime fresh core factors and gives
max_j tau_j^sharp >= (tau^sharp)^(1/4).


Hence on the new residual,
max_j tau_j^sharp
> B^(1/24-xi/4-epsilon_f/4).                          (177.16)


If a maximal fresh core is relative, j in {1,2,3}, M3-T11-027 supplies the squared Gaussian ideal modulus
M_j=(G_j^sharp)^2
with
N(M_j)>=(tau^sharp)^(1/2)
> B^(1/12-xi/2-epsilon_f/2).                          (177.17)


If the maximal fresh core is the all-same core j=0, the retained valuation identity instead supplies a square divisor (G_0^sharp)^2 of the normalized Gaussian numerator with the same norm lower bound (177.17).


Thus the K=1 small-fresh branch from M3-T11-027 is now disposed at an explicit power threshold. The remaining unit-median problem has a guaranteed polynomial fresh conductor and splits into the retained relative-squared-modulus or all-same-square-divisor cases.


This is not yet an analytic counting theorem. In particular, do not discard the triple-spin / torus-double-lift principal-incidence selector to obtain a relaxed separated count, and do not multiply the two M3-T11-027 branches.


8. Scope, novelty and limits


CARD-INDEX searches for D_min=tau, unit median, low median, occupied tau and moving tau found no prior card stating the K=1 receiver collapse or the small-fresh endpoint sector. M3-T11-174 contains the fixed-D_min theorem; M3-T11-176 contains the K=1 chart and content outer budget; their combination (177.2)-(177.4) was not previously recorded.


M3-T11-027 explicitly left the small-fresh branch open pending a cover-conditioned friable/support theorem. Equation (177.11) supplies such a support theorem only because K=1 forces the nonfresh support into 2h with h<=C. No analogous conclusion is claimed for general low median K>1.


The proof is deductive from retained exact identities and an elementary Rankin bound. No physical endpoint enumeration and no independent hostile audit are claimed.

PRIMARY_GATE_CLOSED=false

9. Drive-only handoff


LATEST_RESEARCH_CARD=M3-T11-177
NEXT_CANDIDATE=M3-T11-178
CURRENT_ATTACK=UnitMedianLargeFreshPrincipalIncidence

Treat separately:
(A) maximal relative fresh core: exact squared Gaussian ideal modulus with norm >B^(1/12-xi/2-epsilon_f/2);

﻿M3-T11-176 — Exact unit-median R502 contents and the endpoint low-median counting receiver

STATUS=PROVED_EXACT_UNIT_MEDIAN_RAW_PROFILE / ENDPOINT_LOW_MEDIAN_COUNT_OPEN
PRIMARY_GATE=OPEN / GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT=0
Authority: fresh MAIN, CARD-INDEX through175, short RESULT-LEDGER, active ROUTE and175/174. Full Gaussian orientation and physical reconstruction are retained. No new global upper bound is claimed.


1. Decision and scope
The proposed first low-median test is h_middle=1. Since contents are positive integers, this forces the sorted content triple (1,1,h).
A new universal calculation sharpens175's bounded nonmaximal contents: the entire primitive R502 cone has EXACT contents
(h_A,h_B,h_C)=(h,1,1), gcd(h,tau_raw)=1,
where H_raw=h and tau_raw=R/H_raw. Thus even unit median content and complete content-freshness of tau leave the accumulating raw obstruction intact. This is not merely a size relabeling: exact prime support and the two normalization valuations are proved below.
On endpoints, the missing face cannot be dropped. Sections4-5 give an exact full-lift/denominator test and identify the remaining moving-tau occupancy with its actual low-median outer budget. The genus-five shape is retained theory in a new low-median chart, not a new uniform curve-count theorem.
No new endpoint upper saving, no new negligible endpoint sector, no global credit. The useful threshold-specific tail and the small-c low-median endpoint count remain OPEN.


2. Exact R502 contents, not just ceilings
Use175 notation on coprime m,n with7/2<m/n<4:
J=(m^2+n^2)(m^2+9n^2),
L=(m^2-n^2)(m^2-9n^2),
F=m^4-2m^2n^2+9n^4,
Fplus=m^4+2m^2n^2+9n^4,
K=4mn(m^2-3n^2),
A=JL, B0=K Fplus, C0=16m^2n^2(m^4-9n^4), D=FJ.
Let b=1 if m,n are both odd, otherwise0; a=1 if3 divides m, otherwise0.
The retained source proves g=gcd(A,B0,C0)=2^(5b)3^(4a), R=D/g.
The new exact formulas are
h=J/(2^(2b)3^(2a)), tau_raw=F/(2^(3b)3^(2a)), R=h*tau_raw, (176.1)
gcd(R,A/g)=h, gcd(R,B0/g)=gcd(R,C0/g)=1,              (176.2)
gcd(h,tau_raw)=1.                                     (176.3)


First prove gcd(R,6)=1.
At2: opposite parity makes F,J odd. If both are odd, F is8 modulo16, so v2(F)=3. Each factor of J has v2=1, so v2(J)=2. Thus v2(D)=5=v2(g).
At3: when3 divides m, write m=3r. Then
F/9=9r^4-2r^2 n^2+n^4,
J/9=(9r^2+n^2)(r^2+n^2).
Both are3-adic units: n is a unit and r^2+n^2 is1 or2 modulo3. Thus v3(F)=v3(J)=2 and v3(D)=4=v3(g).
If3 does not divide m, F and J are3-adic units, whether or not3 divides n. Hence R has neither prime2 nor prime3.


Now gcd(D,A)=J*gcd(F,L). Reducing F modulo m^2-n^2 and m^2-9n^2 gives8n^4 and72n^4. Since n is a unit, gcd(F,L) has no prime above3.
At2 it has valuation3b: F has valuation3 when both are odd and each difference of odd squares in L is divisible by8. At3 it has valuation2a: if3 divides m, m^2-9n^2 has valuation at least2 and F has exactly2; otherwise F is a3-unit.
Therefore gcd(F,L)=2^(3b)3^(2a). Dividing gcd(D,A) by g proves h_A=h in(176.1).


The proved175 ceilings give
gcd(D,B0) <=4*81*576*36*72,
gcd(D,C0) <=16*81*144*288,
AND their factor-by-factor gcd proofs show that these gcds have prime support contained in{2,3}. The support conclusion comes from the divisibility/reduction proofs, NOT from numerical size inequalities alone. After division by g, h_B and h_C divide R, which is coprime to6. Hence h_B=h_C=1.
Finally F modulo the two factors of J is12n^4 and108n^4. Thus gcd(F,J) also has support only on{2,3}. Both h and tau_raw divide R and are coprime to6, so gcd(h,tau_raw)=1. This proves all formulas universally.


3. The sharper raw-mask obstruction
By XG-007 on the actual two-face orientation,
c_raw=h_A*h_B=h, H_raw=h, D_min=tau_raw,
D_A=tau_raw, D_B=R.                                  (176.4)
The face complementary to C0 is not assumed integral, although the numerical label R/h_C equals R.
Reuse156's height-shell carrier from175. On >=k B^(1/4) distinct primitive raw edges with R asymp B,
h asymp sqrt(B), tau_raw asymp sqrt(B).
ALL of them have h_middle=1 and gcd(H_raw,tau_raw)=1.
Therefore for fixed delta_D,delta_H,s>0,
sum_{raw R<=B:
     h_middle=1, gcd(H_raw,tau_raw)=1,
     D_min>B^(1/3-delta_D), H_raw>B^(1/3-delta_H)}
     c_raw^s
>= const_s B^(1/4+s/2).                               (176.5)
The172 square-root uncapped-moment incompatibility survives these exact additional masks.
This does NOT refute a useful threshold-specific raw tail. It does NOT refute small-c low-median counting: this carrier has c_raw asymp B^(1/2), outside c_max<=B^(1/6+xi).
R502 perfect-endpoint exceptions are finite by the retained source/173 argument. No raw lower population is transferred to endpoints, and Sigma is not assigned to arbitrary raw points. This finishes the R502 mask diagnostic; another renamed mask card is not the next attack.


4. Exact endpoint full lift when the two smaller contents are1
Relabel an endpoint so h_1=h_2=1,h_3=h. Then
R=h*tau, D_1=D_2=R, D_3=tau.
Its third primitive space triangle is
u=e_3/h, v=f_12/h, u^2+v^2=tau^2, gcd(u,v)=1.
For fixed(u,v,tau), let alpha=u/tau, rho=v/tau, with alpha,rho>0 and alpha^2+rho^2=1.
Put x=e_1/f_12. Full endpoint compatibility requires rational positive b0,c0,d0 satisfying
b0^2=1-x^2,
c0^2=alpha^2+rho^2*x^2,
d0^2=1-rho^2*x^2,                                    (176.6)
and normalized edges
(e_1/R,e_2/R,e_3/R)=(rho*x,rho*b0,alpha).             (176.7)
These are exactly the three physical faces together with the sphere, not three independent random tests.


Over the algebraic closure the three quadratic radicands have six distinct branch points:
+/-1, +/-i*alpha/rho, +/-1/rho.
Their squareclasses are independent because each has its own branch pair. Thus the connected degree8 cover of the x-line has6 branch points, each with inertia2. Riemann-Hurwitz gives
2g-2=-16+6*4=8, hence g=5.
This is a full-lift chart, not a new genus-five counting result. The projection
z=b0*d0, z^2=(1-x^2)(1-rho^2*x^2)
is precisely174/170's genus-one over-cover. Keeping only this product square loses the individual rational square requirements and the middle radicand c0.


For a rational positive point of(176.6), define
R0=lcm(den(rho*x),den(rho*b0),tau)
using reduced positive denominators.
The integral edges R0*(rho*x,rho*b0,alpha) are primitive: the norm-one sphere identity forces any common edge prime to divide R0, which would permit a smaller common denominator. Their space diagonal is exactly R0.
For any reduced rational e/R0, gcd(R0,e)=R0/den(e/R0). Consequently the EXACT unit-content test is
den(rho*x)=den(rho*b0)=R0.                             (176.8)
The third content is then h=R0/tau, uniquely recovered; physical height is R0<=B.
Conversely(176.6),(176.8), positivity and height reconstruct an endpoint with content triple(1,1,h), up to deterministic sign/order choices.
Thus h is not a free scaling variable after a normalized point is fixed. This is the174 reconstruction mechanism, now with its exact two-unit denominator filters exposed.


5. What actually moves, and the correct low-median outer budget
Fixing h does NOT fix tau or rho. The genus-one/genus-five fixed-direction arguments cannot be summed for free over tau. The full Gaussian packet remains:
N(B_1)=N(B_2)=h, N(B_3)=1,
tau=tau0*tau1*tau2*tau3 with pairwise coprime full core norms.
The norm1 coefficient is a unit; it does not set any of the moving relative cores G_1,G_2,G_3 to1.
Keep r_i=conj(epsilon_i)*conj(B_i/conj(B_i))*q_i^2,
Q=q0*q1*q2*q3,
conj(A0)*U^2+2U+A0=0, A0=r_1^2+r_2^2+r_3^2, U=Q^2.
The triple-spin square relation, torus double lift, Gaussian norms, denominator tests and physical masks must ALL stay in the moving-tau occupancy measure. Retained017 bounds a fixed(h,tau) endpoint fiber by B^o; it does not bound the number of active tau for fixed h.


More generally sort contents a<=b<=d, impose b<=K and c_max=b*d<=C.
Then b<=min(K,sqrt(C)). The number of labeled content triples is at most
6*sum_{b<=min(K,sqrt(C))} sum_{a<=b} floor(C/b)
<=6 C min(K,sqrt(C)).                                (176.9)
Pairwise coprimality only reduces this count; coefficient orientations multiply it by B^o.
For K=1 the outer budget is C, rather than the general C^(3/2).
Define A_low(B;C,K) to be the occupied ordered content-tau packets in this exact endpoint subpopulation, including large Sigma, large D_min and all retained physical masks. Then
|A_low| <=P_labeled<=B^o |A_low|.                     (176.10)
For C=B^(1/6+xi),K=B^kappa<=sqrt(C), a SUFFICIENT uniform per-content endpoint/active-tau bound is
B^(1/6-xi-kappa-epsilon), fixed epsilon>0,
or a summed occupied-packet bound <=B^(1/3-epsilon).
For K=1 this is an exponent below1/6-xi, not the general fixed-content1/12 target. It is a less demanding scoped gate, NOT a proved upper bound and NOT scalar-relabel progress credit.
Bare little-o support multiplied by unspecified B^o is insufficient, as171 already corrected.


6. Verification, novelty and limits
INDEX searches for h_middle, median, R502, low and genus-five found174/175 and the retained genus-five lift003, but no exact R502( h,1,1 ) formula with gcd(h,tau)=1. Source primitive gcd and156 count are reused; the universal content formulas and exact freshness mask are new relative to the retrieved portfolio.

The universal polynomial reductions and valuations above are the proof; finite checks are supporting verification. No perfect endpoints enumerated, no independent hostile audit.
The genus-five chart/denominator test and outer budget are deductively verified. No global curve theorem, uniform moving-tau sparsity, or endpoint saving is inferred from them.

Count the endpoint occupied(h,tau) measure using the FULL Gaussian triple-spin/double-lift and(176.8), or produce a proved same-measure averaging adapter. Aim for the section5 summed fixed-power target, not another fixed-fiber theorem.
No further R502 curve classification or raw-mask-only cards are warranted absent a material endpoint-population bridge. The large-c threshold-specific tail remains a separate OPEN branch.

﻿M3-T11-175 — Large primitive-space-direction masks retain the R502 raw moment obstruction
CARD_ID=M3-T11-175
STATUS=PROVED_JOINT_RAW_MASK_OBSTRUCTION / ENDPOINT_CORRELATION_OPEN
PRIMARY_GATE=OPEN / GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT=0
Authority: fresh MAIN, INDEX through174, short RESULT-LEDGER, active ROUTE control and174. Only the retained R502 formulas,156 carrier and173/174 scope are used.


1. Decision and new statement
174 removes the endpoint sector D_min<=B^(1/3-delta_D). The remaining two-direction correlation must therefore be tested on large primitive-space directions, rather than assuming that the new cutoff automatically removes the raw obstructions.
This card proves a quantitative negative result on the exact physical RAW measure:
for every fixed delta_D>0,delta_H>0 and s>0,
sum_{e in E(B):
       D_min(e)>B^(1/3-delta_D),
       H_raw(e)>B^(1/3-delta_H)} c_raw(e)^s
>= const_s B^(1/4+s/2).                          (175.1)
D_min on a raw object means min_i R/gcd(R,e_i). A direction whose complementary face is not integral is not being called a primitive Pythagorean triangle. On the retained R502 carrier, the minimizing direction DOES have an integral complementary face; the second integral space direction is also above the cutoff.


More precisely, a subfamily of >=k B^(1/4) distinct primitive raw edges with R in [kappa_0 B,B] has two actual primitive-space hypotenuses
D_A asymp B^(1/2), D_B asymp B,                   (175.2)
and
c_raw asymp B^(1/2), R/c_raw asymp B^(1/2),
D_min asymp B^(1/2), H_raw asymp B^(1/2).          (175.3)
All constants are independent of B. The constants below are intentionally coarse.
Thus the ordinary square-root-budget raw moment method remains impossible after BOTH large-D and high-H raw masks. No endpoint lower population, no failure of the useful single-threshold tail, and no endpoint upper improvement is proved.


2. R502 notation and existing height bound
For coprime m,n in7/2<m/n<4, put
J=(m^2+n^2)(m^2+9n^2),
L=(m^2-n^2)(m^2-9n^2),
F_-=m^4-2m^2n^2+9n^4,
F_+=m^4+2m^2n^2+9n^4,
K=4mn(m^2-3n^2).
Then the retained raw edges and space diagonal are
A=JL, B0=KF_+, C0=16m^2n^2(m^4-9n^4), D=F_- J.
Write g=gcd(A,B0,C0), R=D/g and
h_A=gcd(D,A)/g, h_B=gcd(D,B0)/g, h_C=gcd(D,C0)/g.
The original source proves g<=2592 and D>=m^8 on the cone. Also D<=240m^8 since n<m. Therefore
m^8/2592<=R<=240m^8.                             (175.4)
The physical faces AC and BC are integral. XG-007 gives
c_raw=h_A h_B, D_A=R/h_A, D_B=R/h_B.              (175.5)


3. New uniform gcd ceilings for the three space contents
The elementary inequality gcd(U,VW)<=gcd(U,V)gcd(U,W) is used throughout.
Because gcd(m,n)=1, n is a unit modulo any divisor of the homogeneous polynomials appearing below.


First,
gcd(D,A)=J*gcd(F_-,L).
Reducing F_- modulo m^2-n^2 and m^2-9n^2 gives8n^4 and72n^4 respectively, so
gcd(F_-,L)<=8*72=576,
h_A<=576J.                                      (175.6)


For B0:
gcd(D,K)<=4*81*576.
Here gcd(D,m)<=81, gcd(D,n)=1, and D modulo m^2-3n^2 is576n^8.
Also
gcd(F_-,F_+)<=36, gcd(J,F_+)<=72,
since the polynomial differences are4m^2n^2 and8m^2n^2, while gcd(F_+,m^2)<=9 and gcd(F_+,n)=1.
Thus
h_B<=gcd(D,B0)
<=4*81*576*36*72=483729408=:K_B.                  (175.7)


For C0 let W=m^4-9n^4. We have
gcd(D,m^2)<=81, gcd(D,n)=1.
Modulo W,
F_- =2n^2(9n^2-m^2),
J=2n^2(5m^2+9n^2).
The gcd of W with9n^2-m^2 divides72. The gcd of W with5m^2+9n^2 divides144: reduce25W modulo that latter linear expression in m^2, obtaining-144n^4.
Therefore
gcd(F_-,W)<=144, gcd(J,W)<=288,
h_C<=16*81*144*288=53747712=:K_C.                 (175.8)


Since J<=20m^4 and m>=1, (175.6)-(175.8) yield
h_max<=K_B m^4.
Together with(175.4),
D_min=R/h_max
>=m^4/(2592 K_B)
>=sqrt(R)/(2592 K_B sqrt(240)).                  (175.9)
This is a uniform lower bound for the raw D_min, not a statement about a missing irrational face.


4. The accumulating carrier lies in a physical height shell
Use exactly156's retained parameter subset:
T=floor((B/240)^(1/8)),
n in(T/8,T/4],
m=4n-k,1<=k<n/2,gcd(k,n)=1.
It has >>T^2 coprime parameters and m>7T/16. The same bounded primitive-object multiplicity<=8 from156 gives >>T^2 distinct raw edges.
Equation(175.4) places them in
const*T^8<=R<=240T^8<=B,
so for sufficiently large B, R>=const*B.
156 gives c_raw>=const*T^4, and the new ceilings give c_raw<=const*T^4. Thus c_raw asymp T^4 asymp sqrt(B).


Since h_B<=K_B, h_A=c_raw/h_B>=const*T^4. Also h_A<=576J<=11520T^4. For large T, h_A exceeds the bounded h_B and h_C. Consequently
h_max=h_A,
D_min=D_A=R/h_A asymp T^4,
D_B=R/h_B asymp T^8.                             (175.10)
Both D_A and D_B are primitive Pythagorean hypotenuses, because their complementary faces BC and AC are integral.
The third D_C need not correspond to an integral face and is not assumed to do so.
Furthermore H_raw=h_A h_B h_C asymp T^4 and R/c_raw asymp T^4, proving(175.2)-(175.3).


Pairwise coprimality of the contents follows from primitive integer edges and the space equation: a prime dividing R and two edges would divide the third edge. Thus exactly
lcm(D_A,D_B)=R, gcd(D_A,D_B)=R/c_raw.              (175.11)
The new carrier therefore inhabits the actual physical two-direction lcm-height window, not an ambient norm-pair box. It is highly unbalanced in direction sizes; its two nonmaximal contents remain bounded.


5. Masked moment consequence and endpoint firewall
Equations(175.3) and(175.10) show that all of these >>B^(1/4) raw edges eventually have D_min>B^(1/3-delta_D) and H_raw>B^(1/3-delta_H). Summing c_raw^s over them proves(175.1).
As in172, a conjectural upper budget B^(1/2+o(1)) for this masked raw moment is impossible for every fixed s>1/2. At C=B^(1/6+xi),0<xi<1/12, Markov needs s>1/(1+6xi)>2/3 to get a fixed-power exponent below1/3. These orders still cannot coexist.
This is new preservation of the obstruction after174's large-D filter; it does not retract174's endpoint small-D theorem.


For actual endpoints, D_i=R/h_i and the174 residual are valid. But the R502 endpoint exceptions are finite by the already-retained source genus-seven argument, as173 records. Hence(175.1) CANNOT be transferred to an endpoint-masked moment.
Sigma is only defined through171's endpoint four-core packet. This card neither defines it on the raw carrier nor claims that the carrier satisfies the actual large-Sigma population. H_raw large is merely a compatible content-size proxy, not that population.


The useful single-threshold raw bound at C=B^(1/6+xi),xi<1/12 remains unrefuted: this quarter-power population is smaller than B^(1/3-xi). A capped moment or a direct tail estimate is not ruled out. No counting gain follows just from the lcm/gcd identities(175.11).


6. Verification and novelty
Fresh INDEX searches for R502 with D_min, two large primitive-space directions and high-content masks found156/173 carrier results and174's new cutoff, but no uniform D_min floor or joint-mask moment lower bound.
Original source height/gcd and156's positive-power carrier count are reused. The new content ceilings and physical-direction profile certify survival after the actual new cutoff. No fixed R502 rational-point classification is attempted.
Exact integer replay checked4939 coprime pairs with n<=180 in7/2<m/n<4 for the three gcd ceilings, R height lower bound, h_max bound and lcm(D_A,D_B)=R. All passed.
The symbolic reductions above prove the ceilings for all coprime cone parameters; replay is supporting verification, not an asymptotic proof. No perfect endpoints were enumerated. Within-session review only; no independent hostile audit.


7. Handoff

Keep both171 large-Sigma and174 large-D conditions, and test the actual missing-third-face/sphere compatibility with the retained full Gaussian orientations. Find a genuine uniform or summed endpoint count, or identify the exact moving-norm cost. Do not transfer a raw lower population to endpoint scope and do not prolong fixed R502 curve classification.
For all moving contents, the needed same-measure two-direction/support theorem remains OPEN; no such theorem was found in this batch. The quarter-power raw obstruction is insufficient to decide the endpoint gate.

﻿M3-T11-174 — Fixed primitive space-hypotenuse fibers and the remaining median-content cost of q_min
CARD_ID=M3-T11-174
STATUS=PROVED_FIXED_SPACE_HYPOTENUSE_BO1_AND_SUMMED_SMALL_D_SECTOR
PRIMARY_GATE=OPEN / GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT=0
CURRENT_ATTACK=EndpointReducedQuotientFiberPreflight
Authority: fresh MAIN, CARD-INDEX through173, short RESULT-LEDGER, active ROUTE control and173. Retained170's exact opposite-face model is the counting input. No new external elliptic theorem is imported.


1. Results and scope
Uniformly for an integer1<=d<=B,
#{primitive positive canonical endpoints R<=B with D_min=d}<=B^o(1), (174.1)
where D_i=R/gcd(R,e_i) and D_min=min_i D_i.
Consequently
P_{D_min<=Z}(B)<=Z B^o(1),                      (174.2)
including every content and direction cost.
For Z=B^(1/3-delta), fixed0<delta<1/3, this sector is o(M3(B)) using the retained lower benchmark M3(B)>>B^(1/3). This is a scoped disposal, not a global upper improvement.


For canonical q=q_min=R/c_max,
m_q(B)<=floor(sqrt(B/q)) B^o(1).                 (174.3)
This is an actual fixed-q estimate, but it does not prove m_q=B^o(1). Its explicit remaining outer coordinate is the median physical content. The fixed-q estimate alone does not dispose of the full small-q/extreme-c sector.


2. One primitive space triangle fixes normalized geometry
Select one direction i, and put
h_i=gcd(R,e_i), u_i=e_i/h_i, v_i=f_jk/h_i, D_i=R/h_i,
where f_jk^2=e_j^2+e_k^2.
Retained004/007 give the primitive Pythagorean triple
u_i^2+v_i^2=D_i^2.
Fix this triple, including its edge/face leg order. Thus
a=u_i/D_i=e_i/R and rho=v_i/D_i=f_jk/R
are fixed positive rationals with a^2+rho^2=1 and0<rho<1.


For an opposite edge set x=e_k/f_jk. Exactly as in170,
1-x^2=(e_j/f_jk)^2,
1-rho^2 x^2=(f_ij/R)^2.
Hence every endpoint lies on
z^2=(1-x^2)(1-rho^2 x^2).                        (174.4)
The branch points +/-1,+/-1/rho are distinct. This is literally170's smooth full-rational-2-torsion family from retained010.
Its model coefficients have height B^O(1), and x has numerator and denominator<=B. The retained uniform bounded-height input therefore bounds the physical rational x by B^o(1), uniformly in this fixed space triangle.
Only that rational-point input is used; no first-cover lift adapter or independent root-line density is imported.


3. Normalized point determines the entire primitive endpoint
For a retained physical x, the normalized edge vector is
(e_i/R,e_j/R,e_k/R)
=(a, rho*sqrt(1-x^2), rho*x),                    (174.5)
with the positive rational square root. Points where either required square is not rational are post-filtered; the genus-one over-cover is used only for an upper bound.
Thus the entire normalized vector is fixed, with at most bounded sign/order choices.


Primitive integer edges determine a unique scale: if two positive primitive integer triples have the same normalized vector, they are rationally proportional; primitivity forces the proportionality factor to be1. Equivalently,
R=lcm(den(e_1/R),den(e_2/R),den(e_3/R))
because gcd(e_1,e_2,e_3)=1.
Therefore no free multiplier h_i, no radial height family, and no remaining content count survives after x is fixed. R, all h_i, tau and every c_i are recovered uniquely.
This is the extra reconstruction observation beyond170's fixed-(r,tau) proof.170 fixed additional labels to recover one h_i by a denominator; here the normalized full vector recovers all contents at once.


Hence a fixed labeled primitive space triangle has B^o(1) endpoint extensions, without fixing tau or a content triple and without restricting to the small-c branch.


4. Fixed D and summed sector
For any fixed D_i=d<=B, the number of primitive oriented Pythagorean triples (u_i,v_i,d) is d^o(1) by the retained sum-of-two-squares divisor count. Three choices of i and finite parity/leg choices are harmless.
Applying Section3 once for each such direction gives (174.1), also when the canonical chosen direction is one attaining D_min.
Summing over the actual integer label d<=Z gives (174.2). This is an endpoint count on exact R<=B, not an ambient rational-height count.
Equivalently, since D_min=R/h_max,
P_{h_max>=R/Z}(B)<=Z B^o(1).                     (174.6)
The threshold here moves with the actual R. Do not replace R by B inside the condition as an equivalence.


This is a space-triangle hypotenuse sector.161 instead bounds short primitive physical-face hypotenuses p_ij=f_ij/gcd(e_i,e_j). Those are different labels. No nonempty perfect-endpoint difference or independence of the two sector savings is asserted. Their union can be removed by addition, with overlap charged once.


5. Exact q_min fiber and median-content outer budget
Sort the physical contents, with deterministic ties,
h_a<=h_b<=h_c, and write tau=R/(h_a h_b h_c).
Retained004 gives exactly
c_max=h_b h_c,
q_min=R/c_max=h_a tau,
D_min=tau h_a h_b=q_min h_b,
R=q_min h_b h_c.                                (174.7)
Thus for a fixed actual q=q_min,
h_b<=sqrt(B/q).                                 (174.8)
Once q and the integer h_b are fixed, D_min=q h_b is fixed. Equation(174.1) bounds the endpoint fiber by B^o(1), including all possible factorizations q=h_a tau and all moving h_c.
Summing over1<=h_b<=floor(sqrt(B/q)) proves (174.3). No additional d(q) polynomial factor is needed; any divisor choices are already inside the fixed-D bound.


If S_q(B) denotes the actual occupied median-content labels in the fiber q, then
|S_q(B)|<=m_q(B)<=B^o(1)|S_q(B)|.                (174.9)
The interval bound(174.8) does not prove sparsity of that support. A uniform subpolynomial fixed-q result would need to control this moving median-content support or provide a stronger correlation theorem. No impossibility of such a theorem is claimed.


The naive outer sum from(174.3) gives
sum_{q<=Q} m_q(B)<=B^(1/2) Q^(1/2) B^o(1),       (174.10)
which does not beat the existing global half-power ceiling for Q>=1. In particular no extreme-c endpoint disposal follows merely by noting q_min<B/C.


After the newly counted sector is removed, the remaining endpoints satisfy
D_min=q_min h_b>B^(1/3-delta).                   (174.11)
For a putative q_min<=Q extreme-c sector this forces h_b>B^(1/3-delta)/Q, with h_c>=h_b. This is a full physical content condition, not two independent congruence savings.
171's independent valid small-Sigma disposal is retained; the current residual has BOTH Sigma>B^(1/3-delta_Sigma) and D_min>B^(1/3-delta_D), together with the earlier exact physical conditions. No multiplicative saving is assigned to their overlap.


6. Dedupe and verification
The fresh index was searched for fixed primitive space hypotenuse, fixed direction, q_min, fixed quotient, two-content and D_min claims.161's short-face sector and170's opposite-face compression were read. The genus-one point theorem is reused; the new conclusions are fixed-D full-scale reconstruction, its globally summed space-hypotenuse sector, and the explicit median-content bound for a fixed q.
Novelty is relative to the retrieved portfolio, not a literature-wide assertion.

﻿M3-T11-173 — R502 elliptic simultaneous-square endpoint lift and high-content raw-mask obstruction
CARD_ID=M3-T11-173
STATUS=PROVED_EXACT_CARRIER_ADAPTER_AND_RAW_MASK_OBSTRUCTION
PRIMARY_GATE=OPEN / GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT=0
Authority: fresh Drive MAIN, INDEX through172, short RESULT-LEDGER, active ROUTE control,172 and the original R502 certificate.171's small-Sigma disposal and endpoint residual are retained.


1. What is new and what is reused
Original Stage25 R502 already proves that the third-face exceptions lie on a squarefree genus-seven curve and are finite. This finiteness is REUSED, not rediscovered progress.156 and172 prove accumulating RAW carrier obstructions, without claiming an accumulating endpoint family.
This card derives an explicit degree-four quotient of that exception curve to a genus-one quartic, with an exact two-shifted-square rational lift. It gives a rational point inside the physical quotient chamber that fails the lift. Separately it proves that a natural high-content raw mask still retains the156 carrier and its172 moment obstruction.
No endpoint upper saving, new negligible endpoint sector, or global closure is claimed.


2. Exact R502 third-face polynomial
Use the reduced rational parameter t=m/n in the fixed cone 7/2<t<4, and the original homogeneous R502 edges A,B0,C0. The normalized polynomials are
a(t)=(t^4-1)(t^4-81),
b(t)=4t(t^2-3)(t^4+2t^2+9),
c(t)=16t^2(t^4-9).
The third-face condition is exactly
y^2=P(t)=a(t)^2+b(t)^2,
P(t)=t^16+16t^14-196t^12+112t^10+5926t^8
     +1008t^6-15876t^4+11664t^2+6561.             (173.1)
This P and its genus-seven squarefreeness are retained from the original R502 source. Primitive division by g does not change rational-square status. Since the primitive edges are integral, a rational third-face diagonal is an integer.


3. New elliptic quotient and exact rational lift
For t!=0 set
u=t^2+9/t^2, w=y/t^4.
Pair reciprocal powers in P/t^8:
t^8+6561/t^8=u^4-36u^2+162,
t^6+729/t^6=u^3-27u,
t^4+81/t^4=u^2-18.
Thus the exact quotient is
E: w^2=Q(u),
Q(u)=u^4+16u^3-232u^2-320u+9616.                 (173.2)
This is a genus-one quartic: gcd(Q,Q') modulo5 is the nonzero constant2, so Q is squarefree over Q. It has the rational point (u,w)=(6,64); calling it genus one does not assert an effective rational-point classification or a rank calculation.
The generic quotient degree is four: t solves t^4-u t^2+9=0, with conjugate values t,-t,3/t,-3/t. The maps t->-t and t->3/t, y->81y/t^8, leave (u,w) invariant.


Crucially the rational parameter lift is EXACTLY
u+6=alpha^2 and u-6=beta^2, alpha,beta in Q.       (173.3)
Forward, alpha=t+3/t and beta=t-3/t.
Conversely (173.3) gives alpha^2-beta^2=12, so t=(alpha+beta)/2 is nonzero rational and 3/t=(alpha-beta)/2. Then u=t^2+9/t^2. Given (u,w) on E, define y=w t^4 to recover (173.1). This proves sufficiency as well as necessity on the finite nonzero chart.
For the positive cone choose alpha>0,beta>0. The chamber is
2545/196<u<265/16,                              (173.4)
because t->t^2+9/t^2 is strictly increasing for t>sqrt(3). The positive root t=(sqrt(u+6)+sqrt(u-6))/2 then lies in (7/2,4).
Therefore physical R502 endpoint parameters correspond precisely to rational (u,w) on E satisfying both shifted-square conditions and this chamber, up to the sign of the face diagonal.


The chamber alone is insufficient, even after solving E:
(u,w)=(16,276) is rational and Q(16)=76176=276^2.
It lies strictly between2545/196 and265/16, but u+6=22 and u-6=10 are nonsquares in Q. It has a positive real parameter in the cone and no rational parameter. This is an explicit elliptic-quotient impostor, not a physical cuboid.
Do not count all rational points of E as R502 endpoints; both shifted-square selectors must be retained. Do not multiply their marginal densities.


4. Endpoint scope and already-known finiteness
The source genus-seven curve has only finitely many rational points by its retained Faltings argument. The exact quotient lift above neither removes that requirement nor strengthens it to an effective classification. Hence R502 contributes only finitely many primitive canonical endpoints at all heights, and so contributes O(1) to any171 endpoint residual. This is a source-to-residual scope adapter, not a new finiteness theorem.
In particular the156 accumulating raw family cannot itself certify an accumulating endpoint obstruction. For each fixed s>0, its endpoint-masked moment is bounded by a constant depending on that finite exceptional set. The raw lower bound from172 cannot be transferred to an endpoint-only moment.
Finiteness for this one fixed polynomial supplies no uniform bound over moving families and no bound for the entire large-c endpoint branch.


5. New high-content raw-mask obstruction
For a primitive space-integral raw object with edges e_A,e_B,e_C and integral faces sharing e_C, define
h_A=gcd(R,e_A), h_B=gcd(R,e_B), h_C=gcd(R,e_C),
H_raw=h_A h_B h_C.
XG-007's two physical space-triangle contents are precisely h_B and h_A: in an integral Pythagorean triple the gcd of its legs equals the gcd of either leg with its hypotenuse. Hence
c_raw=h_A h_B, and H_raw>=c_raw.                  (173.5)
This uses only the two integral faces and the space diagonal. It does not assume the third face or a four-Gaussian-core decomposition.


On the156 carrier with R<=B and c_raw>=kappa sqrt(B),
H_raw>=kappa sqrt(B).
For every fixed delta>0, all these edges eventually satisfy
H_raw>B^(1/3-delta).                             (173.6)
Therefore for fixed s>0 the masked raw moment
sum_{e in E(B), H_raw>B^(1/3-delta)} c_raw(e)^s
>=const_s B^(1/4+s/2).                           (173.7)
The uncapped square-root-budget obstruction of172 survives this high-content raw mask unchanged.


On an actual endpoint, H_raw is171's H and Sigma=H*mu with mu>=1, so H>B^(1/3-delta) implies Sigma>B^(1/3-delta). The high-H part is a subset of the endpoint residual, not the whole residual. A raw high-H envelope for that part still includes the156 carrier.
Sigma itself is not defined on arbitrary raw objects through171's endpoint four-core decomposition. Do not pretend (173.6) puts the raw carrier in the actual Sigma population. It only shows why a content-size proxy cannot remove the raw obstruction. The third-face/lift mask matters.


6. Verification and dedupe
Fresh CARD-INDEX search covered R502, high-content raw masks, fixed quotient, third-face square, and genus-seven carriers. The source already contains P and finiteness. No retrieved card states (173.2)-(173.4), the chamber impostor, or (173.7). Novelty is relative to these retrieved materials, not a literature-wide claim.
Exact integer arithmetic checked9511 coprime pairs with n<=250 and7/2<m/n<4. With U=m^4+9n^4, V=m^2 n^2:
U^4+16U^3V-232U^2V^2-320UV^3+9616V^4=A^2+B0^2,
U+6V=(m^2+3n^2)^2, U-6V=(m^2-3n^2)^2.
It also checked the actual primitive normalization, c_raw=h_A h_B and H_raw>=c_raw. All passed.
Polynomial Euclidean arithmetic modulo5 gave gcd(Q,Q')=2. Direct exact arithmetic checked Q(6)=4096, Q(-6)=1024, Q(16)=76176 and the chamber bounds.
Finite replay supports the symbolic proofs; it does not prove asymptotic distribution or enumerate perfect endpoints. Within-session review only; no independent audit.

﻿M3-T11-172 — R502 obstruction to uncapped square-root-budget cross-gcd moments
CARD_ID=M3-T11-172
STATUS=PROVED_MOMENT_METHOD_OBSTRUCTION / THRESHOLD_TAIL_OPEN
GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT=0 / PRIMARY_GATE=OPEN
CURRENT_AUTHORITY=Drive MAIN, CARD-INDEX, short RESULT-LEDGER, active ROUTE and171.
This card continues171 branch(A), retaining Sigma>B^(1/3-delta). It proves a quantitative obstruction to a proposed raw certificate; it proves no new endpoint upper bound.


1. Measure and retained inputs
Let E(B) be the exact primitive physical Stage14 raw two-face graph edges with integral space diagonal R<=B. Let c(e)=c_raw(e), and for fixed s>0 put
M_s(B)=sum_{e in E(B)} c(e)^s.
Multiplicity is the same physical graph measure as156; no ambient parameter or M3 weight is substituted.
Retained156 supplies constants k,kappa>0 and >=k B^(1/4) distinct edges with c(e)>=kappa B^(1/2), for every sufficiently large B. Retained Stage14 supplies |E(B)|<=B^(1/2+o(1)).
The lower-bound family need not satisfy the third-face-square predicate. Nothing here places it inside171's endpoint residual.


2. New moment obstruction
For every fixed s>0,
M_s(B)>=k kappa^s B^(1/4+s/2).                  (172.1)
This follows by summing only the156 carrier edges.
Consequently a square-root-budget moment theorem
M_s(B)<=B^(1/2+o(1))                            (172.2)
is impossible for every fixed s>1/2. At s=1/2 the lower and upper exponents coincide; no existence of such an upper theorem is asserted.


For the useful threshold C=B^gamma, gamma=1/6+xi, 0<xi<1/12, Markov and (172.2), if available, would give
E_{c>C}(B)<=B^(1/2-s gamma+o(1)).                (172.3)
A fixed-power improvement below the retained M3 lower benchmark B^(1/3) requires
s gamma>1/6, equivalently s>1/(1+6xi)>2/3.       (172.4)
But (172.2) requires s<=1/2 by (172.1). These are incompatible.
Even taking the largest non-refuted order s=1/2 gives certificate exponent
1/2-gamma/2 >3/8 >1/3.                         (172.5)
Thus the entire untruncated c^s moment method with the unstratified square-root budget cannot close branch(A), throughout the useful threshold interval. This rejects a method, not the single-threshold tail conjecture. It is stronger than merely prohibiting the all-C uniform 1/C tail.


For a different proposed upper exponent alpha_s, the necessary carrier constraint is alpha_s>=1/4+s/2. Markov needs alpha_s-s gamma<1/3. A necessary condition for such a certificate is therefore
s(1/2-gamma)<1/12.                              (172.6)
This is only necessary, not sufficient. Improved low-order moments with alpha_s<1/2, or endpoint/residual-masked moments, are not ruled out. The positive-power margin absorbs B^o(1), as corrected in171.


3. Threshold-capped receiver and its limits
Define on the same raw measure
W_s(B;C)=sum_{e in E(B)} min(c(e),C)^s.
Exactly
W_s(B;C)=s integral_0^C u^(s-1) E_{c>u}(B) du,
and E_{c>C}(B)<=C^(-s) W_s(B;C).                (172.7)
The integral is a finite-sum layer-cake identity; the strict inequality at a single boundary has no effect on the integral.
At C=B^gamma<kappa sqrt(B),156 now forces only
W_s(B;C)>=k B^(1/4+s gamma).                    (172.8)
A conjectural W_s<=B^(1/2+o(1)) is not contradicted by this carrier when s gamma<=1/4; Markov would close when s gamma>1/6.
The compatibility window is
1/(6 gamma)<s<=1/(4 gamma).                     (172.9)
It is nonempty. For example s=5/(24 gamma) has carrier lower exponent11/24, and a hypothetical square-root upper budget would give tail exponent7/24<1/3.
No capped upper theorem is proved. The elementary bound W_s<=C^s|E(B)| only returns E_tail<=B^(1/2+o(1)); truncation itself creates no saving. Other raw families can impose further restrictions. An endpoint-specific mask also avoids (172.1) only after a genuine measure adapter; the raw carrier is not known to survive that mask.
A capped moment bound is a distribution theorem including the low-c population, and can be stronger than a desired one-threshold tail. Treat it as an optional certificate, not an equivalent reformulation of the tail and not a new bound.


4. Exact quotient event and correction to CROSS-GCD wording
Retained XG-008 says q=H3/gcd(H2,H3)=R/c_raw on the exact4bn pair measure. Therefore the exact large-c event is
c_raw>C iff q<R/C.                             (172.10)
With R<=B this implies q<B/C. The reverse implication does not follow: q<B/C only gives c_raw>CR/B, which is weaker if R<B.
The route's fixed B/C quotient receiver is sufficient as an upper bound on a superset, but its wording as an equivalent event/formulation is superseded. Dyadic physical-height shells Q<R<=2Q must retain q<R/C for exact counting; q<2Q/C is a sufficient relaxation. Do not discard the moving physical height or confuse a superset count with exact tail measure.
This logical correction does not retract the XG-008 identities.


5. Review and novelty
Targeted CARD-INDEX search for moment, capped/truncated moment, cross-gcd, and156 found the156 carrier lower bound and the general request for a stratified moment, but no (172.1)-(172.6) order incompatibility or capped compatibility window. Novelty is relative to the retrieved Stage37 portfolio, not a literature-wide claim.
The proof is an elementary consequence of the retained156 physical lower bound and Markov's inequality; no new external theorem is invoked. Within-session review checked quantifier order (fixed s,xi then B limit), strict exponent margins, constants, raw/endpoint scope and the capped identity.

These arithmetic checks are illustrations; the symbolic inequalities above prove all0<xi<1/12. No physical endpoints were enumerated and no independent audit is claimed.
