records.title: M3-T11-170 — Opposite-face genus-one compression removes the moving-content fiber
records.content:
﻿SCOPE CORRECTION BY M3-T11-171
The fixed-pair theorem and removal of C^(1/2) loss are retained. Bare support o(B^(1/3)) alone does not absorb a B^o(1) fiber factor. Use a fixed power margin or an explicit occupancy-weighted/envelope condition. Details and countermodel are in171 section7.


M3-T11-170 — Opposite-face genus-one compression removes the moving-content fiber


CARD_ID: M3-T11-170
CANONICAL_CARD_KEY: M3-T11-170
STATUS: PROVED_EXACT_FIXED_PAIR_BO1_UPGRADE / OPPOSITE_FACE_GENUS1_COMPRESSION / GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT=0
GLOBAL_OPERATION: ACTIVE_T11_RESEARCH_WITH_SCOPED_DECOMPOSITION
PRIMARY_GATE: M3-T11-GATE-001, OPEN
GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT: 0
AUDIT_MODE: WITHIN_SESSION_DEDUCTIVE_FROM_RETAINED_010_168_169


1. Current authority and decision


Current MAIN, CARD-INDEX, RESULT-LEDGER, active ROUTE and M3-T11-169 were read first. The needed retained cards M3-T11-004/006/007/010/168/169 were checked only where needed.


Card169 isolated one remaining polynomial factor in the fixed-(r,tau) endpoint fiber: the moving content h_i of length O(r/sqrt(tau)). This card proves that this interval loss is not intrinsic. A second physical face, together with the already-fixed selected space triangle, puts the residual motion on exactly the same full-rational-2-torsion genus-one family already used in retained M3-T11-010. The reduced denominator of one normalized edge then recovers h_i uniquely.


Result: on the live branch r<tau, the fixed-(r,tau) exact endpoint multiplicity is B^o(1), improving M3-T11-168 equation (168.13), which had the weaker C^(1/2)B^o bound.


2. Selected primitive space triangle


Fix an exact primitive canonical endpoint and the canonical face i selected by the global maximum Euclid root r. Write, as in 168,


h_i=gcd(R,e_i),
u_i=e_i/h_i,
v_i=f_jk/h_i,
D_i=R/h_i=c_i*tau,


so


u_i^2+v_i^2=D_i^2,


where f_jk^2=e_j^2+e_k^2 and {i,j,k}={1,2,3}.


Fix (r,tau).


As in 168, after fixing the bounded face/sign/parity choice, the companion Euclid root s satisfies


s^2 == -r^2 mod tau.


Therefore the number of possible positive s<=r is


(1+r/tau) B^o(1).                                  (170.1)


Once s and the finite parity/orientation data are fixed, the primitive space triangle (u_i,v_i,D_i) is fixed. Hence


rho := v_i/D_i = f_jk/R


is fixed, with


0<rho<1.


Also c_i=D_i/tau is fixed. Since c_i=h_j*h_k and h_j,h_k are coprime, the ordered choice (h_j,h_k) costs only


d(c_i)=B^o(1).                                      (170.2)


3. Exact opposite-face genus-one point


For one of the two opposite-face edges, say e_k, define


x := e_k/f_jk.


Every physical endpoint satisfies


1-x^2
=
(f_jk^2-e_k^2)/f_jk^2
=
e_j^2/f_jk^2,


so 1-x^2 is a rational square.


Also


rho*x
=
(f_jk/R)*(e_k/f_jk)
=
e_k/R.


Therefore


1-rho^2*x^2
=
1-(e_k/R)^2
=
f_ij^2/R^2,


which is also a rational square.


Consequently every endpoint maps to the rational genus-one over-cover


z^2=(1-x^2)(1-rho^2*x^2).                          (170.3)


This is exactly the same one-parameter full-rational-2-torsion family used in retained M3-T11-010.


Because 0<rho<1, the four branch points are distinct; there is no rho=0 or rho=1 degeneration on the positive selected space-triangle locus.


The rational height is physical:
rho=v_i/D_i has numerator and denominator <=B,
x=e_k/f_jk has numerator and denominator <=B.


Hence the same uniform bounded-height rational-2-torsion theorem already retained and used in M3-T11-010 applies to (170.3), uniformly in the present physical rho. The number of rational x of physical height <=B^O(1) is therefore


B^o(1).                                             (170.4)


Only the rational-point count from retained010 is used here. Its first-cover lift adapter is not imported.


4. One genus-one point recovers the residual content h_i


For a fixed rational point x, put


t := rho*x = e_k/R.


Reduce t to lowest terms. Since by definition


h_k=gcd(R,e_k),


the reduced denominator of t is exactly


den(t)=R/h_k=D_k.                                   (170.5)


By the endpoint content identities,


D_k=c_k*tau
   =h_i*h_j*tau.


At this stage h_j and tau are already fixed by Sections 2 and the fixed pair (r,tau). Therefore


h_i = den(t)/(h_j*tau).                             (170.6)


Thus one rational genus-one point determines the formerly-moving content h_i uniquely whenever the divisibility and positivity filters required by a physical endpoint hold.


Once h_i is fixed,


R=h_i*D_i


is fixed,
e_i=h_i*u_i is fixed,
e_k=t*R is fixed,
and e_j is fixed up to sign by


e_j^2=f_jk^2-e_k^2,


with f_jk=h_i*v_i.


The positive canonical endpoint therefore has only O(1) reconstructions from the fixed packet and x. All remaining face-integrality, primitivity and canonical-order conditions are post-filters.


5. Upgraded fixed-(r,tau) fiber theorem


Combining (170.1), (170.2), (170.4) and the O(1) reconstruction gives


m_(r,tau)(B)
:=
#{exact primitive canonical endpoints at R<=B
  with canonical global max Euclid root r
  and common residual tau}


<=
(1+r/tau) B^o(1).                                  (170.7)


This strictly improves the retained M3-T11-168 bound


m_(r,tau)
<=
(1+r/tau)(1+r/sqrt(tau)) B^o(1).


On the current live small-c branch, retained168 already gives r<tau for fixed small eta,xi with eta+(5/2)xi<1/4. Hence


m_(r,tau)(B) <= B^o(1).                             (170.8)


The C^(1/2)=B^(1/12+xi/2) pair-fiber loss in 168/169 is removed.


M3-T11-168 is not retracted: its theorem remains correct; (170.7)-(170.8) are a stronger successor bound.


6. Consequence for the support bridge of M3-T11-169


Let P_rt(B;C) be the occupied (r,tau) support and A_ht(B;C) the active labeled content-tau support defined in169.


Retained017 gives


deg_A <= B^o(1).


The new theorem gives on the live branch


deg_P <= B^o(1).


Therefore the two occupied supports are power-equivalent:


|P_rt(B;C)| <= B^o(1)|A_ht(B;C)|,                  (170.9)


|A_ht(B;C)| <= B^o(1)|P_rt(B;C)|.                  (170.10)


In particular,


#E_sc(B;C)
<=
B^o(1)|P_rt(B;C)|.                                 (170.11)


Thus a rigorously sufficient raw occupied-support target, with the retained subpolynomial fiber factor absorbed, is


|P_rt(B;C)|<<B^(1/3-delta), fixed delta>0.           (170.12 corrected by171)


There is no longer an extra C^(1/2) payment for routing through (r,tau).


Equivalently, the weighted support W_rt of169 remains a valid upper-bound device but is no longer the minimal receiver; its r/sqrt(tau) weight was an artifact of stopping before the opposite-face genus-one compression.


7. Relation to the retained fixed-content active-tau route


The 169 firewall is sharpened as follows.


M3-T11-015 through019 still do NOT by themselves prove an occupied-support deficit. Their triple-spin selector remains a fixed-content/coefficient arithmetic selector and the active-tau theorem is still open.


However, if a future theorem proves a fixed-content active-tau support bound, passing between that support and occupied (r,tau) support now costs only B^o(1), not C^(1/2).


For example, the old sufficient hypothetical bound


A_tau(B;h1,h2,h3) << B^(1/12-delta0)


would still give directly


#E_sc
<=
C^(3/2) B^(1/12-delta0+o(1)),


and the pair-support route now reproduces the same power exponent rather than the weaker C^2 bound recorded in169.


So the two live formulations are now losslessly interchangeable at power scale:


- fixed-content active-tau support;
- occupied canonical (r,tau) support.


Neither support deficit is proved here.


8. Why the genus-one compression is not double charging


The new saving is not obtained by multiplying the two appearances of h_i from M3-T11-006/007.


The data used are:


- the selected space triangle fixes rho=f_jk/R;
- the actual opposite face gives 1-x^2 square;
- the actual adjacent face gives 1-rho^2 x^2 square;
- their product places x on one retained010 genus-one curve;

Thus one physical h_i is charged once through one rational-point coordinate. The duplicate cyclic appearances of h_i remain uncharged.


No root-line density modulo h_i^2 is used.


9. Audit and scope


The algebraic identities in Sections 3-4 are direct physical equalities:
x=e_k/f_jk,
rho=f_jk/R,
rho*x=e_k/R,
den(e_k/R)=R/gcd(R,e_k)=D_k=h_i*h_j*tau.


The genus-one model (170.3) is literally the retained M3-T11-010 family z^2=(1-x^2)(1-rho^2*x^2), with physical 0<rho<1 and polynomial physical height. The uniform B^o rational-point input is therefore not a new external theorem import.


CARD-INDEX searches for “opposite face ratio”, “e_k/f_jk”, “selected space triangle”, “fixed max root”, “residual content denominator”, “den(t)=D_k” and “genus-one opposite face” found no prior card stating this adapter.


No physical perfect endpoint was enumerated and no finite example is asserted. The proof is deductive from retained exact identities plus retained010 bounded-height counting. Audit is within-session, not an independent hostile audit.


10. Handoff

(B) c_max<=C on retained R>B^(2/3-eta):
occupied canonical pairs (r,tau) satisfy
gcd(r,tau)=1,
tau>B^(5/12-o(1)),
r^2>B^(7/12-o(1)),
r^2*tau>B^(1-o(1)),
and now each fixed pair has only B^o(1) physical endpoints.


Hence branch(B) reduces to the occupied support cardinality
|P_rt(B;C)|,
with sufficient target |P_rt|<<B^(1/3-delta), fixed delta>0; alternatively an explicit fiber envelope times |P_rt| must be o(B^(1/3)).


Equivalent power-scale route: bound active labeled content-tau support via the retained015-019 selector. The former moving-h_i C^(1/2) transfer loss is gone.


Next research should attack the occupied support itself, preferably by translating the canonical (r,tau) pair into the retained active-tau/triple-spin selector without introducing a new polynomial packet count. If no support theorem emerges, return to branch(A) threshold-specific large-c tail.

﻿M3-T11-171 — Content-weighted two-smallest relative-core divisor and summed endpoint sector


CARD_ID: M3-T11-171
CANONICAL_CARD_KEY: M3-T11-171
STATUS: PROVED_EXACT_FIXED_SIGMA_FIBER / SUMMED_SMALL_SIGMA_ENDPOINT_SECTOR / SUPPORT_QUANTIFIER_CORRECTION
PRIMARY_GATE: M3-T11-GATE-001, OPEN
GLOBAL_OPERATION: ACTIVE_T11_RESEARCH_WITH_SCOPED_DECOMPOSITION
GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT: 0
AUDIT_MODE: WITHIN_SESSION_DEDUCTIVE_FROM_RETAINED_015_016_017_030_170
UNIFORM_ELLIPTIC_INPUT: retained016; no new external theorem imported
PHYSICAL_ENDPOINTS_ENUMERATED: 0


1. Decision and current authority


MAIN, CARD-INDEX, current short RESULT-LEDGER, latest170/169 and the needed individual015-019/010/030 cards were read. Only the relevant ROUTE17-19, 28 and corrected030 interfaces were used; old history was not restarted.


The occupied (r,tau) support is still not counted. Instead, retained016 permits a useful global aggregation of its fixed-two relative-core theorem: include the entire physical content product in a scalar conductor and omit the largest relative norm. This gives a new exactly counted endpoint sector, with all content and coefficient costs included.


Separate correction: bare support little-o is not sufficient when the only fiber control is B^o(1). The fixed-pair theorem of170 and its power-scale support comparison are retained; its bare little-o sufficient target is corrected below.


2. Exact divisor coordinate


For one primitive positive canonical endpoint write
h_i=gcd(R,e_i),
H=h_1 h_2 h_3,
R=H tau,
c_i=h_j h_k.


Use retained015 full (not merely fresh) four-core orientation decomposition
tau=tau_0 tau_1 tau_2 tau_3,
N(G_i)=tau_i.
The four tau_i are pairwise coprime, and G_i are primitive Gaussian integers.


Fix the standard positive Euclid representative for each oriented space triangle, a primary-prime convention, and the finite unit/parity conventions. Factor c_i and tau with the same orientation as that representative. These rules make a canonical packet for each endpoint. Alternatively any bounded/divisor-many retained cover gives the same upper bounds.


Let j be the smallest label attaining max(tau_1,tau_2,tau_3), and let {a,b}={1,2,3}\{j}, a<b. Define
mu=tau_a tau_b,
Sigma=H mu.


Then exactly
Sigma=H*(tau_1 tau_2 tau_3)/max(tau_1,tau_2,tau_3)
     =R/(tau_0 tau_j).                            (171.1)


In particular Sigma is a positive integer divisor of the actual physical R:
Sigma | R,  1<=Sigma<=R<=B.                       (171.2)


This is a canonical physical label, not an ambient root-line or an auxiliary modulus. No fresh-prime assumption is needed.


3. Uniform fixed-Sigma endpoint fiber


Fix Sigma=n. The positive integers
(h_1,h_2,h_3,tau_a,tau_b)
satisfy
h_1 h_2 h_3 tau_a tau_b=n.
There are at most d_5(n)=n^o(1) ordered possibilities. The omitted index j costs at most three choices.


After these five integers are fixed, the three coefficient norms c_i=h_j h_k are fixed. The number of primitive Gaussian B_i with N(B_i)=c_i, with the finite unit/parity choices retained, is B^o(1) by the sum-of-two-squares divisor bound. The representations of the two fixed relative norms tau_a,tau_b likewise cost B^o(1).


Thus the coefficient packet and G_a,G_b are fixed at divisor-many cost. By cyclic symmetry of retained016, the remaining relative core G_j has only B^o(1) endpoint-compatible possibilities.


The retained016 hypothesis check is essential. The pair of actual phases r_a,r_b is neither equal nor opposite on a positive endpoint: opposite phases give opposite physical normalized legs; equal phases force a zero leg through the triple-spin relation and sphere equation. The genus-one quartic is therefore nondegenerate. Its resultant is
Res_t(Q_a,Q_b)=-16(a-b)^2(ab+1)^2,
Q_a(t)=(1-a^2)(1-t^2)+4at.
Model coefficients and point coordinates have physical polynomial height. The uniform rational-torsion input already retained in016 therefore applies, including as content varies over n<=B. The adjective "small" attached historically to the content packet is not needed for this height check: c_i<=R<=B for every endpoint.


Once all three relative cores and the coefficient packet are fixed, set
A=r_1^2+r_2^2+r_3^2,
U=Q^2,
Q=q_0 q_1 q_2 q_3,
q_i=G_i/conj(G_i).
Retained015 gives
conj(A) U^2+2U+A=0.
If A=0 this would force U=0, impossible on the norm-one torus. Otherwise there are at most two U, finitely many Q, and finitely many q_0.


A rational q_0 determines its primitive Gaussian representative G_0 up to units: equality G/conj(G)=G'/conj(G') implies G/G' is rational, and primitivity removes rational dilation. Thus G_0 contributes O(1), not a free radial norm family.


The whole packet fixes tau and R=H tau, and the primitive space directions reconstruct the positive edges up to finite parity/sign choices. All sphere, face-integrality, actual-gcd and canonical-order checks are post-filters.


Consequently, uniformly for n<=B,
m_Sigma(n;B)
=#{primitive canonical endpoints with R<=B and Sigma=n}
<=B^o(1).                                        (171.3)


This proof includes the content budget inside d_5(n). There is no additional C^(3/2) outer factor. It uses one fixed-two elliptic count once and does not multiply cyclic congruence densities.


4. Summed small-Sigma sector


For every 1<=Z<=B,
P_{Sigma<=Z}(B)<=Z B^o(1).                         (171.4)


Hence, for any fixed delta>0,
Z=B^(1/3-delta)
gives
P_{Sigma<=Z}(B)<=B^(1/3-delta+o(1))=o(M3(B)),      (171.5)
using the already-retained denominator lower bound M3(B)>>B^(1/3).


This is a new scoped endpoint disposal, valid before the large-c/small-c split. It is not a global upper improvement or a proof of P/M3->0.


Comparison to corrected030: fixed full R_rel=tau_1 tau_2 tau_3 had divisor-many multiplicity per content packet. Here the largest relative norm is not fixed: retained016 counts it. Simultaneously H is included inside Sigma, so summing over content triples is charged at divisor cost. The content-weighted condition H R_rel<=Z implies Sigma<=Z; the new condition can also admit packets with much larger tau_j. No nonempty physical difference is asserted.


5. Sharpened necessary relative-core balance on the residual


After removing (171.5), every remaining endpoint satisfies
H*tau_(1)*tau_(2)>B^(1/3-delta),                   (171.6)
where tau_(1)<=tau_(2)<=tau_(3) are the three relative norms.


On branch(B), c_max<=C gives H<=C^(3/2). Thus
tau_(1) tau_(2)>B^(1/3-delta)/C^(3/2).             (171.7)


For C=B^(1/6+xi),
tau_(1) tau_(2)>B^(1/12-delta-(3/2)xi),           (171.8)
and therefore both tau_(2),tau_(3) exceed
B^(1/24-delta/2-(3/4)xi).                         (171.9)


Choose delta+(3/2)xi<1/12 when a positive exponent is desired.


This is a full-relative-core condition. It does not assert that each fresh part has the same size; content-supported prime powers remain retained. It also does not authorize multiplying two squared-modulus savings.


For branch(A) the universally valid residual condition is (171.6), without the small-c simplification.


6. Occupied-support bridge


On any retained branch let S_Sigma be the actual occupied canonical Sigma values. Every value is realized by an endpoint, and (171.3) gives
|S_Sigma|<=#endpoints<=B^o(1)|S_Sigma|.             (171.10)


On live branch(B), retained170 also gives the same estimate with P_rt, and retained017 gives it with A_ht. Thus Sigma support, occupied (r,tau) support and active content-tau support have the same power exponent. This comparison alone proves no support sparsity.


The remaining branch(B) problem can be stated as a support count on Sigma>B^(1/3-delta), with the existing retained large-R and small-c conditions and (171.7). All labels refer to the same physical endpoints.


7. Corrected quantifiers in169/170


From N(B)<=K(B)|S(B)| with K(B)=B^o(1), the assertion
|S(B)|=o(B^(1/3))
does not alone imply N(B)=o(B^(1/3)).
For example K(B)=ceil(log B), |S(B)|=floor(B^(1/3)/K(B)) has subpolynomial fibers and little-o support, but weighted mass/B^(1/3)->1. This is an abstract logical countermodel, not a physical population.


A rigorously sufficient power-scale target is instead
|P_rt(B;C)|<<B^(1/3-epsilon), fixed epsilon>0.     (171.11)


The same fixed-power target works for S_Sigma or A_ht. More generally, an explicit envelope K_170(B) is sufficient together with
K_170(B)|P_rt(B;C)|=o(B^(1/3)).
An exact occupancy-weighted sum o(B^(1/3)) is also sufficient.


Retained170 equations170.7-170.11, opposite-face compression and C^(1/2) loss removal remain accepted. Only the automatic bare little-o sufficiency in170.12 and its handoff is superseded. The analogous bare weighted little-o implication in169.9 and crude little-o version169.10 also require absorption of the retained B^o factor; use a fixed power margin or an explicit envelope. The fixed-content active-tau target B^(1/12-epsilon) in015-019 already includes such a margin and remains valid.


8. Verification, novelty and limits


CARD-INDEX was checked for two-smallest relative norms, relative-core norm-product budget, fixed-R_rel, complementary divisor, all-same core and support-quantifier claims. Corrected030 fixes all three relative norms through R_rel. It does not state fixed H*tau_(1)*tau_(2) fibers or the globally summed (171.4).


Exact polynomial determinant verification checks the retained016 resultant. Exact rational arithmetic verifies 2000 triple-spin discriminant identities. Primitive Gaussian phase recovery was checked for 19119 representatives of norm<=20000; 10000 synthetic norm bundles check Sigma|R, (171.1), mu^3<=R_rel^2 and the median/max bounds; 300 integer labels check the ordered-five-factor d_5 formula. These tests verify algebra and finite combinatorics only. They do not prove the uniform elliptic theorem or enumerate physical endpoints. No independent hostile audit is claimed.


Companion files: verify_m3_t11_171.py and M3-T11-171-verification.json, retained in the Stage37 research area.


9. Handoff


LATEST_RESEARCH_CARD=M3-T11-171
NEXT_CANDIDATE=M3-T11-172
CURRENT_ATTACK=ThresholdSpecificLargeCrossGcdTailAfterSmallSigmaDisposal


No occupied-support deficit was proved in this batch. In accordance with170's fallback, next examine branch(A), c_max>B^(1/6+xi), using the actual threshold and the residual Sigma>B^(1/3-delta). Read156 and the CROSS-GCD route only as needed. The false all-C raw B^(1/2)/C target remains prohibited.


Branch(B) remains available through the now-equivalent occupied supports and the full two-large-relative-core necessary condition. Reopen a core-count approach only with a genuine occupied-support/correlation theorem including all content costs, not another fixed-fiber reparameterization.

records.content:
﻿M3-T11-169 — Occupied (r,tau) weighted-support bridge and moving-content firewall


CARD_ID: M3-T11-169
CANONICAL_CARD_KEY: M3-T11-169
STATUS: PROVED_EXACT_INCIDENCE_BRIDGE / WEIGHTED_PAIR_SUPPORT_GATE / FIXED_CONTENT_TRANSFER_FIREWALL / GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT=0
GLOBAL_OPERATION: ACTIVE_T11_RESEARCH_WITH_SCOPED_DECOMPOSITION
PRIMARY_GATE: M3-T11-GATE-001, OPEN
GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT: 0
AUDIT_MODE: WITHIN_SESSION_DEDUCTIVE_FROM_RETAINED_017_168


1. Current authority and purpose


Current MAIN, CARD-INDEX, RESULT-LEDGER, active ROUTE and M3-T11-168 were read first. Retained M3-T11-015 through 019, M3-T11-006, M3-T11-156 and M3-T11-167 were checked only where needed.


The live small-c branch is the retained large-R branch with
c_max<=C,
R>B^(2/3-eta),
tau>B^(5/12-eta-(3/2)xi),
canonical global maximum Euclid root r,
gcd(r,tau)=1,
r^2/tau<=2C,
r^2*tau>const*B^(1-2eta-2xi).


For fixed small eta,xi satisfying eta+(5/2)xi<1/4, M3-T11-168 proves r<tau for all sufficiently large B.


This card asks whether the old fixed-content active-tau/triple-spin route 015-019 automatically gives a new bound for the occupied (r,tau) support. The answer is no. The exact bridge below shows the remaining polynomial cost and identifies the missing theorem.


2. Two support sets and the incidence graph


Let E_sc(B;C) be the exact primitive canonical endpoints in the current small-c, retained-large-R branch.


Define the occupied pair support
P_rt(B;C)
:=
{(r,tau): some endpoint in E_sc(B;C) has canonical max Euclid root r and common residual tau}.


Define the active labeled content-tau support
A_ht(B;C)
:=
{(h1,h2,h3,tau): some endpoint in E_sc(B;C) has these labeled contents and tau}.


Join p=(r,tau) in P_rt to a=(h1,h2,h3,tau) in A_ht if at least one exact endpoint realizes both labels.


This is a same-endpoint incidence graph. No ambient pair or divisor tuples are inserted.


3. Degree on the fixed-content side


Retained M3-T11-017 proves that for each fixed labeled content triple (h1,h2,h3) and fixed tau, the number of exact endpoint candidates is B^o(1), because the three primitive Pythagorean hypotenuses
D1=tau*h2*h3,
D2=tau*h1*h3,
D3=tau*h1*h2
are fixed and each has only divisor-many oriented primitive Pythagorean directions.


Every adjacent canonical r must be realized by one of those exact endpoints. Therefore uniformly,


deg_A(h1,h2,h3,tau) <= B^o(1).                       (169.1)


Consequently,


|P_rt(B;C)| <= B^o(1) |A_ht(B;C)|.                  (169.2)


Thus passing from active fixed-content/tau packets to occupied (r,tau) pairs never creates a support saving by itself.


4. Degree on the fixed-(r,tau) side and the exact residual moving content


M3-T11-168 proves the same-measure fixed-pair endpoint bound


m_(r,tau)(B)
<=
(1+r/tau)(1+r/sqrt(tau)) B^o(1).                    (168.12)


Every distinct active labeled content packet adjacent to (r,tau) contains at least one such endpoint. Hence


deg_P(r,tau)
<=
(1+r/tau)(1+r/sqrt(tau)) B^o(1).                    (169.3)


On the current branch r<tau, this becomes


deg_P(r,tau)
<=
(1+r/sqrt(tau)) B^o(1).                              (169.4)


The proof of168 identifies exactly where the polynomial factor comes from:


- after fixing selected face/sign/parity and (r,tau), the companion Euclid root s has only B^o(1) possibilities because s^2==-r^2 mod tau and r<tau;
- then the selected content c_i is fixed up to B^o(1);
- its coprime factorization c_i=h_j*h_k has only B^o(1) choices;
- the only remaining polynomially long content coordinate is h_i, with
  h_i <= 2*sqrt(2)*r/sqrt(tau);
- after h_i is fixed, D_j,D_k are fixed and the remaining oriented primitive directions cost only B^o(1).


Therefore the factor r/sqrt(tau) is not an anonymous loss. It is the length of one explicit residual moving-content coordinate h_i, up to absolute/subpower factors.


Using r^2/tau<=2C,


deg_P(r,tau) <= C^(1/2) B^o(1),                     (169.5)


and hence


|A_ht(B;C)| <= C^(1/2) B^o(1) |P_rt(B;C)|.          (169.6)


Together, (169.2) and (169.6) give the exact power-scale comparison


P_rt  <= A_ht * B^o,
A_ht   <= C^(1/2) * P_rt * B^o.


The two supports differ by at most the single residual h_i dimension.


5. Weighted occupied-pair reduction


Summing the fixed-pair bound (168.12) over the actually occupied pair support gives the exact same-measure upper bound


#E_sc(B;C)
<=
B^o(1) *
sum_{(r,tau) in P_rt(B;C)}
(1+r/tau)(1+r/sqrt(tau)).                            (169.7)


On the live branch r<tau,


#E_sc(B;C)
<=
B^o(1) *
sum_{(r,tau) in P_rt(B;C)}
(1+r/sqrt(tau)).                                     (169.8)


Define the weighted occupied support


W_rt(B;C)
:=
sum_{(r,tau) in P_rt(B;C)}
(1+r/sqrt(tau)).


Then a sufficient same-measure closure theorem for branch(B) is simply


W_rt(B;C)=o(B^(1/3)).                                (169.9)


This is the correct pair-support target. Replacing W_rt by the crude bound C^(1/2)|P_rt| is legal but loses the information that small c_max pairs carry smaller fiber weight.


At the standard C=B^(1/6+xi), the crude raw-cardinality sufficient condition is


|P_rt(B;C)|
=
o(B^(1/4-xi/2)).                                     (169.10)


No such raw support bound is currently proved.


6. Why M3-T11-015 through 019 do not automatically remove the weight


M3-T11-015 works after fixing a labeled content triple and its small Gaussian coefficient packet. It writes
D_i=tau*c_i,
A_i=B_i Z_i,
N(B_i)=c_i,
N(Z_i)=tau,
then decomposes the equal-norm tau parts Z_i into the four relative-orientation cores G_0,G_1,G_2,G_3. The triple-spin and six-bilinear selectors of 015-019 act on this fixed-content/coefficient packet.


For the fixed-(r,tau) fiber above, after c_i=h_j*h_k is fixed, the residual h_i changes
c_j=h_i*h_k,
c_k=h_i*h_j.


Thus varying h_i changes the norms and orientations of the two small coefficient factors B_j and B_k. It is not motion purely inside the equal-tau cores G_0,...,G_3.


Therefore the fixed-content triple-spin selector cannot be summed over the h_i interval for free. A new theorem would be required that is uniform in this one moving content/coefficient parameter.


This is exactly the kind of same-measure two-edge correlation that M3-T11-006 left open: one physical content is seen simultaneously in the two neighboring directions, and the two appearances may not be multiplied as independent savings.


Accordingly:


OLD_FIXED_CONTENT_TRIPLE_SPIN_AUTOMATIC_PAIR_SUPPORT_SAVING = false.


This is a transfer firewall, not a rejection of 015-019. Those cards remain valid and remain a direct route on the fixed-content side.


7. Quantitative comparison of the two routes


Retained M3-T11-015/017 give the old direct fixed-content budget


# labeled content triples
<=
C^(3/2+o(1)).


The sufficient old gate is a uniform fixed-content active-tau bound


A_tau(B;h1,h2,h3)
<<
B^(1/12-delta0)


for some fixed delta0>0.


If such a theorem is proved, direct counting through M3-T11-017 gives


#E_sc
<=
C^(3/2) B^(1/12-delta0+o(1)).                       (169.11)


At C=B^(1/6+xi), the exponent is


1/3 + (3/2)xi - delta0.


Thus the old route closes by taking xi sufficiently small compared with delta0.


If the same hypothetical fixed-content bound is first translated to pair support using only (169.2), and then the crude pair fiber C^(1/2) is paid, one gets only


#E_sc
<=
C^2 B^(1/12-delta0+o(1)).                           (169.12)


At the standard scale its exponent is


5/12 + 2xi - delta0.


So routing 015-019 through the raw (r,tau) support loses exactly the residual C^(1/2) moving-content dimension and is strictly weaker than using the active-tau theorem directly.


This proves the route decision:


- use 015-019 directly if attacking fixed-content active tau;
- use the (r,tau) route only if a genuinely new theorem controls W_rt or the residual h_i motion;
- do not claim that the near-B size of r^2*tau plus the old triple-spin selector automatically yields pair-support density.


8. New narrow gate


The new pair-side theorem target can be stated in either equivalent useful form.


Weighted-support form:
CyclicOccupiedRTauWeightedSupport:
W_rt(B;C)=o(B^(1/3)).


Residual-content form:
CyclicFixedRTauMovingContent:
for occupied (r,tau), control the realized residual h_i in
h_i <= 2*sqrt(2)*r/sqrt(tau)
with a same-measure average saving beyond the trivial interval length.


A strong pointwise theorem
# realized h_i for fixed (r,tau) <= B^o(1)
would upgrade the fixed-pair endpoint fiber to B^o(1), but this strong statement is NOT proved here.

﻿M3-T11-168 — Global-max Euclid-root/content equivalence and R2tau amplification

STATUS: PROVED_EXACT_GLOBAL_MAX_ROOT_AMPLIFICATION / FIXED_PAIR_FIBER_BOUND / GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT=0

1. Current authority and decision


Current MAIN, CARD-INDEX, RESULT-LEDGER, active ROUTE and M3-T11-167 were read first. The retained large-R branch, M3-T11-013/014, and the older fixed-content active-tau cards M3-T11-015 through 019 were checked only where needed.


The current variable r below is the canonical global maximum among the six positive Euclid roots introduced in M3-T11-167. It is not the norm-one torus coefficient r_i used in M3-T11-015/016.


This card proves three new exact statements:
(1) r^2/tau is equivalent up to an absolute factor 2 to the largest cyclic content c_max;
(2) the product of the three reduced space hypotenuses is R^2*tau, forcing a much stronger lower bound on r on the retained large-R/small-c branch;
(3) fixing the pair (r,tau) leaves at most a square-root-content physical fiber, not an arbitrary polynomial fiber.


No global endpoint power saving is claimed.


2. Local Euclid-root size versus one content


For each primitive space triangle
u_i^2+v_i^2=D_i^2,
D_i=c_i*tau,
write the two positive coprime Euclid roots from M3-T11-167 as a_i,b_i, and put
t_i=max(a_i,b_i).


If u_i is even,
D_i=a_i^2+b_i^2.
If u_i is odd,
D_i=(a_i^2+b_i^2)/2.


In both parity cases one has the uniform absolute comparison


D_i/2 <= t_i^2 <= 2D_i.


Let
r=max(t_1,t_2,t_3)
and let
c_max=max(c_1,c_2,c_3).


Choose i_* with t_i*=r. Then
r^2 <= 2D_i* <= 2 c_max*tau.


On the other hand, choose j with c_j=c_max. Since
t_j^2 >= D_j/2,
we have
r^2 >= t_j^2 >= c_max*tau/2.


Therefore the exact global comparison is


c_max/2 <= r^2/tau <= 2 c_max.        (168.1)


Thus the ratio r^2/tau is not a new independent large parameter: it is the existing maximum cyclic content, up to a bounded factor.


In particular:
- c_max>C implies r^2/tau>C/2;
- c_max<=C implies r^2/tau<=2C.


This gives a direct translation between the current Euclid-root language and the old cross-gcd/content split.


3. Three-hypotenuse product identity


Retain
c_1=h_2*h_3,
c_2=h_1*h_3,
c_3=h_1*h_2,
H=h_1*h_2*h_3,
R=H*tau.


Since D_i=c_i*tau,


D_1*D_2*D_3
=
(c_1*c_2*c_3)*tau^3
=
H^2*tau^3
=
R^2*tau.                                      (168.2)


Because every local maximum t_i is <=r and D_i<=2t_i^2<=2r^2,


D_1*D_2*D_3 <= 8r^6.


Combining with (168.2),


r^2 >= (R^2*tau/8)^(1/3)
     = (1/2) R^(2/3) tau^(1/3).               (168.3)


This inequality is on the exact same endpoint. No face independence is used.


4. Strong amplification on the retained small-c branch


On the branch
c_max<=C,
the exact cyclic product identity also gives


H^2=c_1*c_2*c_3<=C^3,
so
H<=C^(3/2),
and therefore
tau=R/H >= R/C^(3/2).                          (168.4)


Putting (168.4) into (168.3) yields the cleaner direct bound


r^2 >= R/(2*C^(1/2)).                          (168.5)


Multiplying by tau gives


r^2*tau >= R^2/(2*C^2).                        (168.6)


Now use the retained large-R branch
R>B^(2/3-eta)
and the standard threshold
C=B^(1/6+xi).


Then every endpoint in the current small-c branch satisfies


tau > B^(5/12-eta-(3/2)xi),                   (retained M3-T11-013)


r^2 > (1/2) B^(7/12-eta-xi/2),                (168.7)


r^2*tau > (1/2) B^(1-2eta-2xi).               (168.8)


This strictly improves the weaker root exponents recorded in M3-T11-167:
the governing lower bound is now r^2>B^(7/12-o(1)), not merely B^(1/4-o(1)),
and the coprime product r^2*tau is at the B^(1-o(1)) scale, not merely B^(2/3-o(1)).


The improvement is an exact amplification of already-retained large-R plus the three simultaneous space triangles. It is not yet a count.


5. Exact global compatibility in normalized legs


Because
e_i=h_i*u_i=(H/c_i)u_i
and
R=H*tau,
the terminal diagonal equation
e_1^2+e_2^2+e_3^2=R^2
is equivalent to


(u_1/c_1)^2+(u_2/c_2)^2+(u_3/c_3)^2=tau^2.    (168.9)


Thus the three primitive space triangles with hypotenuses D_i=c_i*tau are not independent choices. Their primitive legs must satisfy the same endpoint sphere after content normalization.


Equation (168.9) is retained as the exact physical compatibility that any future (r,tau)-support count must preserve. It is consistent with, and is the elementary physical-coordinate form underlying, the older equal-tau/triple-spin receiver M3-T11-015 through 019.


No new credit is taken from (168.9) alone.


6. Fixed-(r,tau) same-measure fiber bound


Fix positive integers r and tau and restrict to endpoints for which r is the canonical global maximum Euclid root.


Choose the selected face and root sign/parity; this costs only an absolute constant.


Let s<=r be the companion Euclid root on the selected face.


In both parity cases integrality of c_i implies


s^2 == -r^2 mod tau.


Because gcd(r,tau)=1 and every prime of tau is split (p==1 mod4), the congruence has at most
2^omega(tau)=B^o(1)
residue classes modulo tau.


Hence the number of possible positive s<=r is at most


(1+r/tau) B^o(1).                              (168.10)


Once s is fixed, c_i is fixed by
c_i*tau=r^2+s^2
in the even-u_i case, or
2*c_i*tau=r^2+s^2
in the odd-u_i case.


The factorization
c_i=h_j*h_k
has B^o(1) ordered coprime choices for (h_j,h_k).


For the remaining h_i, global maximality of r gives
D_j,D_k<=2r^2,
hence


h_i*h_k*tau<=2r^2,
h_i*h_j*tau<=2r^2.


Therefore


h_i <= 2r^2/(tau*max(h_j,h_k)).


Since max(h_j,h_k)>=sqrt(c_i), while the selected-face comparison gives
c_i>=r^2/(2tau), one obtains


h_i <= 2*sqrt(2)*r/sqrt(tau).                  (168.11)


For fixed h_i,h_j,h_k,tau, the remaining D_j,D_k are fixed primitive Pythagorean hypotenuses. By the standard divisor/Gaussian representation bound, their oriented primitive directions contribute only B^o(1) candidates. The endpoint sphere and reconstruction constraints are post-filters.


Consequently


m_(r,tau)(B)
:=
#{exact primitive canonical endpoints with canonical max root r and common residual tau}
<=
(1+r/tau)(1+r/sqrt(tau)) B^o(1).               (168.12)


On the current small-c branch, (168.1) gives
r^2/tau<=2C.


Moreover, for fixed small eta,xi satisfying
eta+(5/2)xi<1/4,
the retained tau lower bound implies tau/C -> infinity, so r<tau for all sufficiently large B.


Then (168.12) simplifies to


m_(r,tau)(B) <= C^(1/2) B^o(1).                (168.13)


At C=B^(1/6+xi),


m_(r,tau)(B)
<=
B^(1/12+xi/2+o(1)).


This is a genuine same-measure fixed-pair fiber theorem. It does not control the number of occupied (r,tau) pairs.


7. Interpretation against the retained active-tau route


M3-T11-017 already proves B^o(1) multiplicity for fixed labeled content triple and fixed tau. The present theorem forgets the content triple and retains only (r,tau), so the residual C^(1/2) fiber cost in (168.13) is expected: one content direction remains movable.


Therefore the pair (r,tau) is a useful compression, but not automatically a stronger receiver than the retained fixed-content active-tau/triple-spin route.


The exact comparison (168.1) shows why:
- the ratio r^2/tau is essentially c_max;
- the scale tau is the old active residual;
- the endpoint sphere/triple-spin selector is still the arithmetic condition deciding which such pairs are physically occupied.


Thus 168 rules out treating the near-B conductor r^2*tau in (168.8) as an independent density gain. A new theorem must bound occupied pair support, or exploit the retained triple-spin selector on that support.


8. Verification and audit limits


The local inequality
D/2<=max(a,b)^2<=2D
is immediate from the exact Euclid formulas and was replayed on all 63638 oriented primitive Pythagorean leg choices with D<=200000.


For synthetic content-compatible bundles, pairwise-coprime h_i and split-prime tau were chosen so that all three D_i=c_i*tau admit primitive Pythagorean representations. Across the generated test set, the replay verified exactly:
- D_1 D_2 D_3 = R^2 tau;
- c_max/2 <= r^2/tau <= 2c_max;
- R^2 tau <= 8r^6;
- on c_max<=C, r^2>=R/(2sqrt(C)).


These bundles are not asserted to satisfy the endpoint sphere and are not physical cuboids. Physical endpoints enumerated=0. The theorem statements follow algebraically from retained004/013/167 plus exact primitive Pythagorean formulas.

2. Every normalized factor in 166 is already a perfect square


Retain one primitive space triangle
u^2+v^2=D^2,
gcd(u,v,D)=1.


If u is odd, then v is even and D is odd. Define
F_- = D-v,
F_+ = D+v.
Then F_-F_+=u^2. Both factors are odd and
gcd(F_-,F_+)=1:
a common divisor divides 2D and 2v, hence is 1 because it is odd and gcd(D,v)=1.
Since the product of two coprime positive integers is a square, there are unique positive coprime integers a,b with
F_-=a^2,
F_+=b^2,
u=a*b.


If u is even, primitive parity gives v,D odd. Define

Current MAIN, CARD-INDEX, RESULT-LEDGER, active ROUTE and M3-T11-165 were read first. Targeted INDEX searches for square divisor / large square divisor / D_i±v_i / Pythagorean factor / space-triangle factor found no prior card for the global physical factorization below.


M3-T11-026 is a packet-specific fresh-tau Gaussian squared-modulus transfer. M3-XD-GATE-001 is a paused moving common-core square-divisor gate. Neither is the theorem below. M3-T11-156 also matters operationally: a uniform raw cross-gcd 1/C tail is false. Therefore branch (A) below must be recorded as the threshold-specific endpoint/raw-edge tail gate, not as an already proved global tail theorem.


This card gives an exact deterministic same-endpoint router. It does not prove a power-saving count.


2. Physical space-triangle normalization


Let (e1,e2,e3) be a primitive canonical endpoint with all three face diagonals integral and terminal space diagonal R integral. A primitive Euler brick has exactly one odd edge and two even edges; hence R is odd.


Retain
h_i=gcd(R,e_i),
u_i=e_i/h_i,
D_i=R/h_i,
c_i=H/h_i=h_j*h_k,
tau=R/H,
where H=h1*h2*h3.


Let f_jk be the physical face diagonal opposite e_i. Retained M3-T11-007 gives
h_i=gcd(R,f_jk),
so
v_i=f_jk/h_i
is integral and


u_i^2+v_i^2=D_i^2.


Moreover gcd(u_i,D_i)=1, hence each (u_i,v_i,D_i) is a primitive Pythagorean triple. Since R and all h_i are odd, u_i has the same parity as e_i: exactly one u_i is odd and two are even.


Define
hat_u_i =
  u_i        if u_i is odd,
  u_i/2      if u_i is even.


Define the two normalized linear factors
F_i,- , F_i,+ by


if u_i is odd:
  F_i,- = D_i-v_i,
  F_i,+ = D_i+v_i;


if u_i is even:
  F_i,- = (D_i-v_i)/2,
  F_i,+ = (D_i+v_i)/2.


Then in every case
F_i,- * F_i,+ = hat_u_i^2
and
gcd(F_i,-,F_i,+)=1.


Also
0<F_i,±<2D_i<=2B.


3. Exact prime-square allocation


Fix i. Because the two normalized factors are coprime and their product is hat_u_i^2, every prime power p^a || hat_u_i occurs with exponent exactly 2a in exactly one of F_i,- or F_i,+.


Now let
Lambda=L_free=lcm(u1,u2,u3).


Because exactly two u_i are even and one is odd, dividing the even u_i by 2 lowers the global 2-adic lcm exponent by exactly one and changes no odd exponent. Therefore


hat_Lambda := lcm(hat_u_1,hat_u_2,hat_u_3) = Lambda/2.


For each prime power p^a || hat_Lambda, choose deterministically the least index i for which v_p(hat_u_i)=a. In that chosen face, the coprime factorization above determines uniquely which sign epsilon in {-,+} receives p^(2a).


For each of the six buckets (i,epsilon), let q_i,epsilon be the product of all p^a assigned to that bucket.


Then the q_i,epsilon are pairwise coprime and satisfy the exact identities


product over the six buckets q_i,epsilon = hat_Lambda = Lambda/2,


q_i,epsilon^2 | F_i,epsilon.


Therefore at least one bucket obeys


q := max q_i,epsilon >= (Lambda/2)^(1/6),


and for the deterministically first maximizing bucket


q^2 | F_i,epsilon,
q^2 >= (Lambda/2)^(1/3).


This is a no-double-charge endpoint router: every endpoint selects one canonical face/sign/bucket.


4. Freshness of the selected square modulus


The selected q divides hat_u_i and hence u_i. Since (u_i,v_i,D_i) is primitive,


gcd(q,D_i)=1.


Because D_i=c_i*tau, this gives


gcd(q,c_i*tau)=1.


Also q^2|F_i,epsilon implies, without any parity exception,


v_i == sigma*D_i mod q^2


for one sigma in {+1,-1}. Equivalently,


v_i == sigma*c_i*tau mod q^2,
gcd(q,c_i*tau)=1.


Thus the selected modulus is an actual content-free square modulus on one physical space-triangle root line. It is not obtained by multiplying independent face densities.


5. Consequence on the current 164/165 core


Retain the equal-cutoff core after 162/163:
all three d_ij>D and all three ell_ij>E.


For any C, M3-T11-164 gives the exact split


(A) some c_i>C;


(B) max_i c_i<=C and
    Lambda=L_free>E^3/C^(3/2),
    gcd(Lambda,tau)=1.


On branch (B), the selected square modulus from Section 3 satisfies


q^2 >= (Lambda/2)^(1/3)
     > 2^(-1/3) * E/C^(1/2).


At the standard scales
E=B^(1/3-delta),
C=B^(1/6+xi),


branch (B) therefore forces


q^2 > const * B^(1/4-delta-xi/2),


q > const * B^(1/8-delta/2-xi/4),


together with one exact physical congruence


v_i == sigma*c_i*tau mod q^2,
gcd(q,c_i*tau)=1.


Hence the live core is now routed to two explicit theorem gates:


(A) threshold-specific large-c_i endpoint/raw-edge tail at C=B^(1/6+xi);


(B) a large fresh square-modulus physical space-triangle root line with modulus q^2>B^(1/4-o(1)).


M3-T11-156 forbids replacing gate (A) by the false uniform raw B^(1/2+o(1))/C theorem. For 0<xi<1/12, the useful threshold-specific C=B^(1/6+xi) tail remains unrefuted but unproved.


6. Relation to previous square-modulus receivers


This branch is structurally analogous to, but not identical with, M3-T11-026 and M3-XD-GATE-001.


- Unlike M3-T11-026, q is selected directly from the global physical L_free support and the congruence is on the elementary physical space triangle (v_i,D_i), not on a fixed-content relative-core Gaussian coordinate.
- Unlike M3-XD-GATE-001, the square modulus q^2 is forced by the current large-L_free branch and is coprime to the corresponding D_i=c_i*tau.
- No existing Fourier coefficient separation or same-measure large-q counting theorem is automatically inherited. An adapter would still be required.


The ambient count of integers F<=2B with some square divisor q^2>=Y is at most O(B/Y^(1/2)), but this is not an endpoint-measure theorem and gives no global credit here.


7. Verification and audit limits


The local normalized factorization was replayed exhaustively on every primitive Pythagorean triple with hypotenuse D<=200000.


There are 31819 unordered triples and 63638 oriented choices of the leg u. For every oriented choice the replay verified exactly:
- F_-*F_+=hat_u^2;
- gcd(F_-,F_+)=1;
- every p^a||hat_u occurs to exponent 2a in exactly one normalized factor.


Additionally, 10000 synthetic three-face parity bundles were formed from one odd-leg primitive triple and two even-leg primitive triples. These are not physical cuboids. For every bundle the deterministic global allocation verified:
- hat_Lambda=Lambda/2;
- product of the six bucket roots equals hat_Lambda;
- each q_i,epsilon^2 divides its assigned F_i,epsilon;
- max q_i,epsilon >= hat_Lambda^(1/6).


These finite tests validate only the arithmetic adapter. Physical endpoints enumerated=0. The exact endpoint statement follows from the proved primitive-space-triangle identities and deterministic prime allocation, not from finite data.

﻿M3-T11-165 — Fixed R-free edge-LCM multiplicity and small-support disposal


CARD_ID: M3-T11-165
CANONICAL_CARD_KEY: M3-T11-165
STATUS: PROVED_EXACT_FIXED_LFREE_FIBER / SMALL_LFREE_SECTOR_DISPOSED / LARGE_TAIL_OPEN
GLOBAL_OPERATION: ACTIVE_T11_RESEARCH_WITH_SCOPED_DECOMPOSITION
PRIMARY_GATE: M3-T11-GATE-001, OPEN

1. Current decision and scope


Current MAIN, CARD-INDEX, RESULT-LEDGER, active ROUTE and M3-T11-164 were read first. Targeted CARD-INDEX searches for fixed lcm / LCM multiplicity / fixed L_free / fixed reduced lcm / common-free support found no prior card for the theorem below. M3-ODD-001 gives fixed unique-odd-edge multiplicity; M3-DIV-001 gives exact odd-edge divisor coordinates. They are related physical anti-concentration results but do not state fixed L_free multiplicity.


This card proves a same-measure fixed-fiber theorem for the R-free edge-LCM from 164 and a small-L_free endpoint-sector bound. It does NOT control the large-L_free tail isolated by 164.


2. Retained notation


For a primitive canonical endpoint with edges e1,e2,e3 and integral terminal diagonal R, retain
h_i = gcd(R,e_i),
H = h1*h2*h3,
tau = R/H.


From M3-T11-004/007/164 define
u_i = e_i/h_i,
D_i = R/h_i,
L_free = lcm(u1,u2,u3).


M3-T11-164 gives
L_free = L/H where L=lcm(e1,e2,e3),
and gcd(L_free,tau)=1.


Let f_jk be the integral face diagonal opposite e_i. Retained M3-T11-007 gives
h_i = gcd(R,f_jk).
Hence
v_i := f_jk/h_i
is an integer and
u_i^2 + v_i^2 = D_i^2,
with gcd(u_i,D_i)=1.


Thus each u_i is a leg of a primitive Pythagorean triangle whose hypotenuse is D_i.


3. Fixed-leg hypotenuse multiplicity


Fix a positive integer u.


Every positive primitive solution
u^2 + v^2 = D^2
satisfies
(D-v)(D+v)=u^2.


If u is odd, both factors are positive odd integers. Every solution determines a factor pair alpha*beta=u^2, alpha<beta, and
D=(alpha+beta)/2,
v=(beta-alpha)/2.


If u is even, primitive parity forces v,D odd. Put
alpha=(D-v)/2,
beta=(D+v)/2.
Then
alpha*beta=u^2/4,
and again the factor pair determines D,v.


Therefore the number of possible primitive hypotenuses D for a fixed leg u is at most
d(u^2),
where d is the divisor function.


No height theorem is used here.


4. Exact fixed-L_free fiber bound


Fix
Lambda := L_free.


Because
lcm(u1,u2,u3)=Lambda,
each u_i divides Lambda. Hence there are at most
d(Lambda)^3
ordered triples (u1,u2,u3).


For each fixed u_i, Section 3 gives at most d(u_i^2) possible D_i. Since u_i|Lambda,
d(u_i^2) <= d(Lambda^2).
Thus the number of possible ordered sextuples
(u1,u2,u3,D1,D2,D3)
is at most


d(Lambda)^3 * d(Lambda^2)^3.


Now use the retained endpoint triangle-content theorem M3-T11-004. For any endpoint-consistent D-triple,
tau = gcd(D1,D2,D3),
c_i = D_i/tau,
and
c1=h2*h3,
c2=h1*h3,
c3=h1*h2.


Therefore the positive h_i are uniquely recovered, when consistent, by
h1^2 = c2*c3/c1,
h2^2 = c1*c3/c2,
h3^2 = c1*c2/c3.


After h_i are recovered,
R=H*tau,
e_i=h_i*u_i,
and the opposite face diagonals are h_i*v_i.
Hence the endpoint is uniquely determined by the sextuple, subject to the remaining physical/canonical consistency filters. Those filters can only remove candidates.


Consequently the exact physical endpoint fiber satisfies


m_Lfree(Lambda;B)
:= #{primitive canonical endpoints at R<=B with L_free=Lambda}
<= d(Lambda)^3 d(Lambda^2)^3.


Since u_i< D_i<=R<=B, we have
Lambda <= u1*u2*u3 < B^3.
The elementary divisor bound therefore gives, uniformly for every Lambda occurring at height B,


m_Lfree(Lambda;B) = B^o(1).


This is a same-measure endpoint anti-concentration theorem. It does not pass through an ambient raw-edge host.


5. Small-L_free endpoint sector


For 1<=Z<=B^3, summing the fixed-fiber bound over Lambda<=Z gives


P_Lfree,small(B;Z)
:= #{endpoints at R<=B with L_free<=Z}
<= Z B^o(1).


Therefore for every fixed delta>0, with
Z=B^(1/3-delta),


P_Lfree,small(B;Z)=o(M3(B))


using the retained lower bound
M3(B) >> B^(1/3).


This sector is not the same statement as M3-T11-163. Card163 controls a small primitive face leg. Card164 converts the complement to large total edge-LCM L. Since
L=H*L_free,
large H can coexist algebraically with small L_free, so the new small-L_free deletion is a distinct physical coordinate deletion. No claim is made that every algebraically possible overlap is occupied by an endpoint.


6. Interaction with the 164 router


The current equal-cutoff core after 162/163 has all three
d_ij>D
and
ell_ij>E.


M3-T11-164 splits this core, for any C, into


(A) some c_i>C;
(B) max c_i<=C and
    L_free>E^3/C^(3/2),
    gcd(L_free,tau)=1.


The present fixed-fiber theorem does not improve the lower bound in branch (B). In the standard scale
E=B^(1/3-delta),
C=B^(1/6+xi),
branch (B) already has
L_free>B^(3/4-3delta-(3/2)xi),
far above the small-support range disposed here.


The useful new information is instead:
- fixed L_free has B^o(1) endpoint multiplicity;
- small L_free is globally negligible without conditioning on c_i;
- any future large-c_i analysis may also delete its small-L_free subbranch at no polynomial cost.


Do not infer that the large-L_free tail is small merely because each fixed fiber is small. The ambient number of possible Lambda values is too large.


7. Verification and audit limits


The fixed-leg factorization in Section 3 was checked exhaustively for every 1<=u<=5000 by two independent arithmetic enumerations:
(1) factor-pair reconstruction from (D-v)(D+v)=u^2, with the even-leg /4 normalization;
(2) primitive Euclid parameter enumeration.


All 5000 fixed-leg sets matched exactly, comprising 9822 primitive leg-hypotenuse incidences. The largest fixed-u incidence count in this range was 16, at u=4620.


This finite replay checks only the arithmetic fixed-leg adapter. Physical endpoints enumerated=0. The fixed-L_free endpoint theorem is proved by the divisor-count argument plus retained M3-T11-004/007/164 reconstruction, not by finite endpoint data. Audit is within-session, not an independent hostile audit.


8. Handoff

NEXT_CANDIDATE=M3-T11-166
CURRENT_ATTACK=LargeLFreeSupportDistributionOrCrossGcdCoupling

P(B) <= P_near(B;D) + P_axis(B;E) + P_core(B;D,E),
with the first two terms o(M3) at D=E=B^(1/3-delta).


The new reusable theorem is
m_Lfree(Lambda;B)
<= d(Lambda)^3 d(Lambda^2)^3
= B^o(1),
and therefore
P_Lfree,small(B;Z)<=Z B^o(1).


Next research must address the distribution/support cardinality of large L_free on the exact endpoint measure, preferably together with one of:
- the existing large-c_i raw-edge cross-gcd tail;
- gcd(L_free,tau)=1 and the exact D_i=c_i*tau space-triangle system;
- the exact odd-edge/divisor chart.


Do not sum B^o(1) fixed-L_free fibers across the full B^3 ambient Lambda range.
Do not multiply c_i or tau appearances as independent savings.
